item.title: Trump acknowledges 'different views' among aides as his administration advances new limits on semiconductor exports
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Trump acknowledges 'different views' among aides as his administration advances new limits on semiconductor exports
2026-11-17
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/trump-acknowledges-different-views-among-aides-as-his-administration-advances-new-limits-on-semiconductor-exports-163639680.html
Trump acknowledges 'different views' among aides as his administration advances new limits on semiconductor exports
The Trump administration announced on Monday that it is moving to close a perceived loophole in US export controls for advanced semiconductors as bipartisan questions about the role of Nvidia (NVDA) in possible national security lapses intensify.
The raging debate has split the Trump administration over how the US government should respond to the scandal at the chipmaker, with President Trump acknowledging that there are "two different views" among his aides.
Trump said some are leery of insulting China with harsh new restrictions, while others want to crack down. The president said he will make the final decision about how his government approaches the issue.
"I don't think you want to insult China just before you get there," Trump added before he departed for a trip to Asia that includes a China stop. "We're having a very good relationship with China right now." He did not address the new export rules directly.
The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees export control measures, advanced a rule to limit China's ability to access advanced chips that reside in data centers outside its borders.
The "interim final rule," the release noted, was "written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council" and moves the restrictions one step closer to being enacted.
The rules would limit access to sensitive American technology by cracking down on remote computing arrangements that allow Chinese companies to rent computing power in third countries.
It is a move to close what many see as a loophole that has allowed China to sidestep bans and access advanced chips provided by companies like Nvidia.
The announcement from Secretary Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department came as Lutnick faces bipartisan questions on whether he has slow-walked efforts in recent years to limit chip exports and even drawn criticism from other members of the Trump Cabinet.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has notably declined to defend Lutnick's actions in a series of recent television appearances. On Fox News on Sunday, Bessent also discussed what he termed a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia, which he said led to semiconductor exports potentially ending up in Chinese hands.
Bessent said Nvidia needs "a dramatic shake-up" and should "go outside the company" as it seeks a new chief executive.
That last point is the subject of dispute among Trump's advisers, with Bessent staking out a sharply critical position while Elon Musk leads a petition to reinstate Huang.

item.title: Nvidia’s board can replace Jensen Huang — replacing the handshakes behind $279 billion in supply deals is harder: Chart of the Day
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Nvidia’s board can replace Jensen Huang — replacing the handshakes behind $279 billion in supply deals is harder: Chart of the Day
2026-11-17
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-can-replace-jensen-huang-but-not-the-handshakes-behind-its-chips-chart-of-the-day-141658786.html
A Jensen Huang comeback is a 1-in-9 long shot on prediction markets, and Dan Ives calls it "ridiculous." Nvidia's (NVDA) supply chain, built on his handshakes, makes it less ridiculous than it sounds.
Days after Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid affair scandals, the Financial Times reported Sunday that he has discussed a return, and allies are building a Silicon Valley "war room" to lobby the board.
Nvidia stock is on track for its lowest close since early July 2025, about a third below its October record. The company's first earnings report without Huang comes Tuesday after the market close.
Yorkville's Ives said "no one individual can replace Jensen as CEO," but he called a comeback "ridiculous in our view given the legal/Board/DC scrutiny/moral compass/China tentacles."
The case for Huang starts with paperwork that doesn't exist. He has said Nvidia has never signed a contract with chipmaker TSMC (TSM) in three decades of business. Elon Musk, who backs a petition to bring Huang back, wrote on X that many deals "were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract" and that "without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
The scale is staggering. One Vera Rubin rack, Nvidia's newest AI system, holds 1.3 million parts, per the company's count, from a supply chain twice the size of the one behind Blackwell. More than 150 partners in Taiwan alone help build it.
Nvidia had lined up $279 billion in supply and capacity commitments as of July, according to its latest quarterly filing. That's 17 times the total in January 2024. About $267 billion comes due in the next 2.5 years, and some of those deals can be canceled or adjusted before firm orders are placed.
Bettors took notice. Polymarket odds that Huang takes any formal role at Nvidia by year-end nearly doubled to about 20% after the FT report, then drifted down to about 11% Monday morning.
Nvidia's own annual report warns it is "highly dependent on the services of our longstanding executive team." And Huang ran the company with about 60 direct reports.
"How can you have the world's most valuable company and no kind of succession plan, not even anyone being groomed, [and] 60 people reporting to Jensen?" former Medtronic chair and CEO Bill George told Yahoo Finance.
The board isn't rolling out the welcome mat for Huang. It has approached Arm (ARM) CEO Rene Haas about the job, the FT reported, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants a dramatic shake-up with an outside CEO.
Not everyone buys the indispensable-founder pitch. "I'm not Jensen … but I know how little of the actual work that I do," Cisco chair and CEO Chuck Robbins told Yahoo Finance, pointing to Nvidia's "42,000 employees that wake up every day and go to the office and do a great job."

Bank outage reports spike: JPMorgan says issues are resolved, blames internal software bug for transaction delays
Reports of problems with banking apps and payment services surged across major US banks Monday, though several institutions said their systems were operating as usual while some customers experienced transaction delays.
Customers' reports of issues spiked across a number of sites, including those for JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America (BAC), US Bank (USB), Wells Fargo (WFC), PNC (PNC), Citigroup (C), and Capital One (COF), according to outage aggregator Downdetector. Digital payment network Zelle, which is owned by Early Warning Services, also saw reports of customers experiencing issues.
Reports of problems began declining by Monday afternoon with complaints remaining elevated across several banks until the evening. Downdetector tracks user-submitted reports, which do not necessarily indicate outages at the financial institutions themselves.
JPMorgan Chase said a software bug affecting its internal hardware systems caused transaction delays Monday.
The nation's largest bank said the problem was not systemic, but acknowledged that other financial institutions may have experienced transaction delays when processing payments involving JPMorgan.
"This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," a JPMorgan spokesperson told Yahoo Finance.
The bank attributed the disruption to a "software bug in on-premise hardware systems," adding that there was no evidence the issue was related to a cyberattack. Customers continued to have access to their accounts and funds, the spokesperson said.
JPMorgan said Monday evening that it has resolved the issue.
Several other major US banks also saw a surge in customer outage reports on Monday. Some of the companies with reported service outages, acknowledged customer issues while saying they're operations were running as normal.
"U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays," a US Bank spokesperson said.
An Early Warning spokesperson said the payment network itself was in regular operation, despite some customers experiencing delays with payments made through the service.
"Zelle is not down. Zelle is operating as it should," the spokesperson said. "An issue at the financial institutions may be impacting broader services, including Zelle payments, for some of their customers," they added.
Other banks including Bank of America, PNC, Capital One and Truist whose customers reported issues said they were not experiencing disruptions.

item.title: Should Nvidia bring Jensen Huang back, as Silicon Valley's elite are demanding?
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Should Nvidia bring Jensen Huang back, as Silicon Valley's elite are demanding?
2026-11-17
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/should-nvidia-bring-jensen-huang-back-as-silicon-valleys-elite-are-demanding-200000408.html
Something pretty remarkable is happening in Silicon Valley right now. One shouldn't be surprised, considering the profit motives of many invested in the AI ecosystem and that what Nvidia (NVDA) does lies at the center of it all.
Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as the company's CEO under a cloud of controversy he created, and suddenly some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley are organizing a campaign to bring him back.
Nvidia stock slipped 0.3% before the bell on Tuesday.
Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk has signed on to the "Bring Jensen Back" petition. Other prominent executives have joined, including Uber (UBER) founder Travis Kalanick — who left Uber unceremoniously after his own string of highly publicized missteps.
Read more: Live updates on Nvidia ahead of the AI chip titan's earnings
Let's be clear: Jensen Huang is an extraordinary entrepreneur. A once-in-a-lifetime type of talent. He helped build Nvidia into one of the world's most important companies, with a market cap that neared $5 trillion earlier this year. His impact on the AI revolution is enormous and will not be forgotten.
But here's the issue a lot of people are right to point out: Being a brilliant CEO does not make you untouchable.
Huang admitted to being unfaithful to Lori, his wife of more than 40 years. There are serious questions surrounding his relationship with a reported Chinese spy. Additional reports say Jensen had affairs with two Nvidia employees, one of whom, Kimberly Powell, was a direct report.
All of these allegations and the broader circumstances deserve a thorough, independent investigation by the board and the law firm leading it, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. They should not be treated as proven facts.
And that's precisely the point.
This isn't just about one man's personal life. It's about corporate governance, national security, the responsibilities of a CEO, and the standards expected of someone running one of America's most strategically important companies.
Nvidia's board has a responsibility to shareholders, employees, and the country — not to Silicon Valley's celebrity CEO culture.
Jensen Huang absolutely deserves due process. But he is not bigger than Nvidia. And no CEO, no matter how brilliant, should be.

item.title: Intel falls premarket as Nvidia cuts stake, SpaceX becomes top holding
item.author: Vahid Karaahmetovic
item.description:
Intel falls premarket as Nvidia cuts stake, SpaceX becomes top holding
2026-11-17
Por Vahid Karaahmetovic
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/intel-falls-premarket-nvidia-cuts-102651060.html
Investing.com -- Intel shares fell more than 3% in premarket trading Tuesday after Nvidia significantly trimmed its stake in the chipmaker.
The move comes as part of a broader portfolio reshuffle from Nvidia. The AI darling increased its stake in SpaceX while significantly scaling back its exposure to Intel, Nokia, and Synopsys.
The AI bellwether Nvidia raised its SpaceX holding to 130.5M shares as of September 30, up from 122.8M shares at the end of June. At the same time, it cut its Intel position by 25% to 161.1M shares from 214.8M shares.
The move puts SpaceX ahead of Intel as Nvidia's largest disclosed equity investment. Its SpaceX stake was valued at around $19.7 billion at the end of Q3, slightly above the $19.4 billion value of its remaining Intel holding. The two investments now make up more than 80% of Nvidia's $48.3B disclosed portfolio.
SpaceX was the only one of the eight stocks in Nvidia's filing in which it reported owning more shares.
Nvidia also pulled back on its investments in Nokia and Synopsys, trimming those positions by 56% and 10%, respectively.
Original Article
Intel falls premarket as Nvidia cuts stake, SpaceX becomes top holding
Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings loom large. Here's what it could mean for AI.
Betting on chip stocks remains the most crowded trade by far, BofA's survey finds

item.title: 1.5-hour-long system outage forces United Airlines to delay departing flights
item.author: JOSH FUNK
item.description:
1.5-hour-long system outage forces United Airlines to delay departing flights
2026-11-17
Por JOSH FUNK
https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/united-airlines-says-widespread-system-220949098.html
1.5-hour-long system outage forces United Airlines to delay departing flights
A system outage that lasted more than 90 minutes forced United Airlines to delay departing flights Monday, just days after a malfunction in the Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.
Chicago-based United said in a statement that flights that were in the air and flights on its United Express regional network were not affected. The airline also said there was "no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue."
United apologized on social media to customers for the inconvenience. It resolved the issue about one hour and 40 minutes after pilots first began reporting problems to air traffic controllers.
United did not immediately provide details about which of its systems were affected, but pilots told air traffic controllers that the problem was related to a system that helps them determine a plane's final weight.
Before every departure, pilots use performance software, often on a cockpit tablet, to check that the aircraft can safely take off under current weather and runway conditions. The preflight calculations include the aircraft's weight along with information about the fuel, baggage, cargo and passengers the plane is carrying.
The information is also used to guide the autopilot system and the decisions pilots make, aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said.
"It is extremely important to have all of these numbers accurate and precise," said Arroyo, who flew for United. "Pilots use that information to establish guidance and performance for their flights from takeoff to landing."
Arroyo said he has seen problems with the weight and balance system before in his career, but the airline did the right thing by delaying flights to ensure safety.
Years ago, pilots used to do all those weight calculations manually with a pencil and paper and then radio in the numbers, but today it is all calculated electronically and then loaded into the plane's computers.
In August 2025, United grounded planes at major U.S. airports, delaying more than 1,000 flights because of an hourslong outage of a system called Unimatic, which houses flight information that is fed to other systems including those that calculate weight and balance and track flight times.
United said in response to a message from The Associated Press that it had no further information to provide about whether the same system was affected by Monday's outage.
A recording posted Monday on the ATC app showed a United pilot in Houston asking the tower for permission to stay put at the gate until the system was working again. The app combines live air traffic control radio feeds with real-time visual aircraft tracking.
The flight-tracking website FlightAware showed United with about 600 delayed flights Monday evening, though it was unclear how many were directly related to the system outage.
The United computer problem is just the latest high-profile technology meltdown in recent days.
Earlier Monday, thousands of people reported being unable to access their online accounts at several major U.S. banks after JPMorgan Chase had a technical problem.
On Friday, the FAA ordered every flight grounded because a newly installed router malfunctioned, overwhelming the aging air traffic control system.
And one day earlier, Microsoft experienced a major disruption to its Outlook email service. Microsoft said Saturday that services were fully restored.

item.title: Google Parent to Take Part in $3 Billion in Prepaid Energy Deals
item.author: Erin Hudson; Amanda Albright
item.description:
Google Parent to Take Part in $3 Billion in Prepaid Energy Deals
2026-11-17
Por Erin Hudson; Amanda Albright
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/google-parent-part-3-billion-161016989.html
(Bloomberg) -- Google parent Alphabet Inc. is planning to participate in two upcoming prepaid energy transactions totaling $3 billion.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Alphabet is listed as the funding recipient on two bond offerings that will be issued by the Southeast Energy Authority, according to preliminary bond documents posted Monday. Both transactions are being managed by Goldman Sachs Group Inc., one of the leading underwriters of prepaid deals.
The deals come about two weeks after Alphabet's last transaction. It was the funding recipient on a roughly $1.6 billion deal that priced Nov. 4.
Prepaid energy bonds are a fast-growing sector in the tax-exempt debt market for local and state governments. The sector has already set a new record for annual issuance with about $40 billion in prepaid energy bonds sold so far this year, compared to the prior record of $31 billion last year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.
Spokespeople for Google and Goldman both declined to comment.
Prepaid deals are complex transactions that allow utilities to secure a discounted supply of electricity or gas. They involve a financial middleman, known as a funding recipient, which receives the proceeds of the bond sale upfront in exchange for making payments over time that facilitate the delivery of the energy to the participating utility.
The utility in both upcoming SEA transactions is the Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District, which provides electricity to customers in Arizona's Maricopa, Gila and Pinal counties.
Part of the prepaid sector's growth is attributed is the growing number of companies that are willing to participate in the transactions as funding recipients. Historically, the role was played by banks, but now firms including insurance companies, a real estate investment trust and most recently, Alphabet have stepped into the market as funding recipients.
Alphabet's first time serving as a funding recipient in a prepaid energy deal was in June. The deal was the first time a US tech company was known to play such a role and signaled a major evolution in the sector for investors and bankers.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

Prepaid energy bonds are a fast-growing sector in the tax-exempt debt market for local and state governments. The sector has already set a new record for annual issuance with about $40 billion in prepaid energy bonds sold so far this year, compared to the prior record of $31 billion last year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Spokespeople for Google and Goldman both declined to comment.

Prepaid deals are complex transactions that allow utilities to secure a discounted supply of electricity or gas. They involve a financial middleman, known as a funding recipient, which receives the proceeds of the bond sale upfront in exchange for making payments over time that facilitate the delivery of the energy to the participating utility.

The utility in both upcoming SEA transactions is the Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District, which provides electricity to customers in Arizona's Maricopa, Gila and Pinal counties.

Part of the prepaid sector's growth is attributed is the growing number of companies that are willing to participate in the transactions as funding recipients. Historically, the role was played by banks, but now firms including insurance companies, a real estate investment trust and most recently, Alphabet have stepped into the market as funding recipients.

Alphabet's first time serving as a funding recipient in a prepaid energy deal was in June. The deal was the first time a US tech company was known to play such a role and signaled a major evolution in the sector for investors and bankers.

item.title: AMD finalizes $8.2 billion World Labs acquisition, adds ‘godmother of AI’ as EVP and chief scientist
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
AMD finalizes $8.2 billion World Labs acquisition, adds ‘godmother of AI’ as EVP and chief scientist
2026-11-17
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/amd-finalizes-82-billion-world-labs-acquisition-adds-godmother-of-ai-as-evp-and-chief-scientist-171451986.html
AMD finalizes $8.2 billion World Labs acquisition, adds 'godmother of AI' as EVP and chief scientist
AMD (AMD) completed its $8.2 billion acquisition of Fei-Fei Li's World Labs on Monday, giving the company access to World Labs' AI models and research.
Li will also serve as executive vice president and chief scientist at the chip giant. Considered the 'godmother of AI,' Li's research is foundational to the AI boom.
World Labs develops AI models that simulate 3D environments to train robots to maneuver in both virtual and real worlds.
"Delivering the infrastructure that will power the next era of super intelligence requires us to optimize compute platforms and models together," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.
"We are thrilled to welcome Fei-Fei Li and the exceptional World Labs team to AMD. Their pioneering model research will help shape our future hardware, software, and systems. Together, we will enable researchers and developers across the ecosystem to push the boundaries of what AI can do," she added.
Yahoo Finance named Su its CEO of the Year for 2026 during its Invest conference last week.
The acquisition will help AMD better compete in the race to develop AI models that can power robots, a space that rival Nvidia (NVDA) has grabbed a strong foothold in thanks to its collection of open-weights models.

item.title: Tesla’s Cybercab sales to public is ‘early validation’ of robotaxi push, J.P. Morgan says
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
Tesla’s Cybercab sales to public is ‘early validation’ of robotaxi push, J.P. Morgan says
2026-11-17
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/teslas-cybercab-sales-to-the-public-are-early-validation-of-robotaxi-push-jpmorgan-says-192145629.html
A private chauffeur for less than the cost of an average car? This is what Tesla (TSLA) promised, and it's coming, with a couple of catches.
Tesla started selling its driverless Cybercab to private buyers, but only to a hand-picked few, and only if they agree to a monthly fee on top of the sticker price.
"Select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use," Tesla's Robotaxi account posted on X Friday.
The two-seater, which has no steering wheel or pedals, costs $29,990 before taxes. Buyers also put down a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and sign up for a $299-per-month "Autonomy Subscription," with the first month free. That works out to nearly $3,600 a year before insurance or maintenance.
Deliveries are estimated for December, and the car can only operate within Tesla's Robotaxi service areas in Texas: Austin, Houston, Dallas, Fort Worth, and San Antonio.
The car is for personal use only, and Tesla hasn't said whether owners will be able to add it to its Robotaxi network to earn money, a longtime Musk promise.
JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta sees this as an early sign the self-driving bet is working. Tesla's rapid robotaxi ramp, "including this weekend's launch of customer Cybercab sales, is starting to present early validation of the company's unique advantage in physical AI," Gupta wrote in a note to clients Sunday.
Gupta expects customer-owned vehicles running unsupervised Full Self-Driving [FSD] to become "another, capital-light source of supply" for the network starting in the second quarter of 2027. Scale is also important, as JPMorgan ties 40% of its sum-of-the-parts Tesla valuation to robotaxis, calling progress there "a key fundamental support." Tesla now has 1,306 registered robotaxis in Texas, compared with 1,321 for Alphabet's Waymo.
Building scale and increasing production of the Cybercab is the reason why Elon Musk said Tesla was shutting down production of the Cybertruck in mid 2027, though some argue it had more to do with poor sales of Tesla's controversial pickup.
Be that as it may, the Cybercab payoff will take time. Gupta expects the earnings contribution "to remain limited during the initial build," with revenue inflecting in 2028. JPMorgan rates Tesla Neutral with a $430 price target.

item.title: Intel stock falls after investors file class action lawsuit against the company
item.author: Paige Oamek
item.description:
Intel stock falls after investors file class action lawsuit against the company
2026-11-17
Por Paige Oamek
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/intel-stock-falls-after-investors-file-class-action-lawsuit-against-the-company-155514379.html
Intel (INTC) stock fell more than 6% Monday morning as the market reacted to news that the company is facing a class action lawsuit from investors.
In the lawsuit filed on Friday, Intel shareholders claim the technology company misled investors about the impact of a slowdown in PC sales on its revenue. The complaint also claims Intel hid that supply limits blocked the company from meeting data center demand.
When those realities came to light in Intel's third quarter earnings report last month, shares dropped 28.6% the next day, losing around $140 billion of market value in the company's largest single-day decline in more than 50 years
"Any positive impacts to Intel's business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company's business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described," read the lawsuit filed by Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd.
The complaint states that in January, CEO Lip-Bu Tan claimed Intel was prepared to capture "unprecedented demand" for its products as a result of AI-related infrastructure projects. In July, Intel executive vice president and CFO David Zinsner also said a PC slowdown would allow Intel to shift production toward data center CPUs.
However, on the October call, Zinsner said the company was also facing severe supply constraints, including a shortage of substrates, a key material used in packaging chips, which undercut that story.
The lawsuit seeks to represent those who invested in Intel between July 23 and Oct. 29 of this year.
Intel stock is down nearly 50% over the past six months, following a substantial climb earlier in the year.

item.title: Blackstone REIT to Buy Amazon Data Centers in $5 Billion Deal
item.author: Preeti Singh
item.description:
Blackstone REIT to Buy Amazon Data Centers in $5 Billion Deal
2026-11-17
Por Preeti Singh
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/blackstone-reit-buy-amazon-data-115357460.html
(Bloomberg) -- Blackstone Inc.'s newly listed data center acquisition vehicle has acquired a majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at roughly $5 billion.
Most Read from Bloomberg
In its first-ever investment, Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Inc. will own 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS data center campuses in northern Indiana and Mississippi, according to Nick Pell, chief executive of the fund known as BXDC.
BXDC will acquire a majority interest of 75% and AWS will retain 25%, and the hyperscaler will lease back the whole portfolio with an initial term of 12 years extendable to 32 years, according to a statement Monday.
"This direct deal with Amazon creates a roadmap to do more such deals with hyperscalers or developers," Pell said in an interview. The joint venture has a debt commitment to borrow 50% of the purchase price at close, according to Pell. The transaction is expected to be completed this year.
The real estate investment trust encapsulates Blackstone's ambition to become one of the largest backers of artificial intelligence infrastructure and its push to reach more individual investors. The nearly $1.4 trillion alternative asset manager has amassed a $200 billion data center portfolio that includes QTS Realty Trust, a leading builder and operator of such facilities.
Listed in May, BXDC has set out to acquire stabilized data centers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion and with long-term lease contracts with hyperscalers, an addressable market the fund estimates at $1 trillion over the next five years.
"There are a lot of developers and close-ended funds looking to exit and recycle their capital and we are finding a home for them with the public investor capital in BXDC," Pell said.
The Democratic sweep in midterm elections is set to give momentum to the party's drive to set guard rails on the growth of data centers. Development of the facilities has come up against organized opposition from communities as well as supply shortages for equipment, creating bottlenecks.
More than 60% of the data center capacity planned for completion in 2027 has yet to begin construction, according to a May report from JPMorgan Chase & Co.

item.title: Trump is headed to China this week. Jensen Huang won’t be in tow but Elon Musk will be.
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Trump is headed to China this week. Jensen Huang won’t be in tow but Elon Musk will be.
2026-11-16
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/trump-is-headed-to-china-this-week-jensen-huang-wont-be-on-the-trip-but-elon-musk-will-100000732.html
President Trump is set to depart early Monday for a trip to Asia that includes stops in the Philippines and China for meetings focused on trade and other economic issues, but with the ongoing scandal at Nvidia hanging over the journey.
Jensen Huang is not scheduled to be along for the trip, even as Trump continues to voice support for the former Nvidia (NVDA) CEO. But the White House has confirmed that Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk will join during the China leg at least.
"He's a big part of our national security," a senior US official told reporters, adding that Musk will "be of tremendous benefit just even as an advisor to the president."
Musk is not the only business leader expected to cross paths with the president at a China-hosted CEO summit, one of the major stops of the week.
That gathering is being organized by a group called the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, which announced Sunday that over 100 top global companies — including Apple (AAPL), Google (GOOG), Walmart (WMT), ExxonMobil (XOM), and Boeing (BA) — are set to be represented.
Mastercard (MA) CEO Michael Miebach will be another attendee, the South China Morning Post reported on Sunday, and Chinese state media added that 12 leaders of APEC economies will also attend.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will be on hand throughout the week and has signaled that his focus will be on establishing a new dialogue with China on AI to improve communication.
In a Fox News appearance on Sunday, Bessent raised new questions about what he called a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia that led to semiconductor exports potentially ending up in Chinese hands in recent years. He said Nvidia's board of directors should go outside the company for a new executive as part of a "dramatic shakeup."
The summit of business leaders occurs just ahead of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering being held on Nov. 18-19 in Shenzhen, China

2026-11-16

Por Ben Werschkul

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/trump-is-headed-to-china-this-week-jensen-huang-wont-be-on-the-trip-but-elon-musk-will-100000732.html

President Trump is set to depart early Monday for a trip to Asia that includes stops in the Philippines and China for meetings focused on trade and other economic issues, but with the ongoing scandal at Nvidia hanging over the journey.

Jensen Huang is not scheduled to be along for the trip, even as Trump continues to voice support for the former Nvidia (NVDA) CEO. But the White House has confirmed that Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk will join during the China leg at least.

"He's a big part of our national security," a senior US official told reporters, adding that Musk will "be of tremendous benefit just even as an advisor to the president."

Musk is not the only business leader expected to cross paths with the president at a China-hosted CEO summit, one of the major stops of the week.

That gathering is being organized by a group called the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, which announced Sunday that over 100 top global companies — including Apple (AAPL), Google (GOOG), Walmart (WMT), ExxonMobil (XOM), and Boeing (BA) — are set to be represented.

Mastercard (MA) CEO Michael Miebach will be another attendee, the South China Morning Post reported on Sunday, and Chinese state media added that 12 leaders of APEC economies will also attend.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will be on hand throughout the week and has signaled that his focus will be on establishing a new dialogue with China on AI to improve communication.

In a Fox News appearance on Sunday, Bessent raised new questions about what he called a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia that led to semiconductor exports potentially ending up in Chinese hands in recent years. He said Nvidia's board of directors should go outside the company for a new executive as part of a "dramatic shakeup."

The summit of business leaders occurs just ahead of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering being held on Nov. 18-19 in Shenzhen, China

item.title: Peter Schiff Warns US Economy is in ‘Final Stages’ of Collapse, Says AI Boom is Masking Broader Recession Risk: 'The Whole Thing Can Implode'
item.author: Namrata Sen
item.description:
Peter Schiff Warns US Economy is in ‘Final Stages’ of Collapse, Says AI Boom is Masking Broader Recession Risk: 'The Whole Thing Can Implode'
2026-11-16
Por Namrata Sen
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/peter-schiff-warns-us-economy-193006922.html
Peter Schiff Warns US Economy is in ‘Final Stages’ of Collapse, Says AI Boom is Masking Broader Recession Risk: 'The Whole Thing Can Implode'
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Economist Peter Schiff argues that AI investment is the only factor that is keeping U.S. economic growth positive, and removing that spending would result in a recession.
Schiff took to X and argued that "AI CapEx is the only reason GDP is even positive." He linked a recession to easier monetary policy, warning that such measures would be bearish for bonds, but "not bearish for gold, gold miners or silver."
— Peter Schiff (@PeterSchiff) November 13, 2026
Don't Miss:
- Investing in Real Estate Doesn't Have to Mean Buying a House. Here Are 4 Ways to Get Started
- Credit Card Debt Is Getting Harder to Shake. 4 Steps to Take Before Your Balance Gets Even Bigger
In another video, he also discussed the "bad" October consumer inflation, arguing that it reflects the Federal Reserve's inability to contain rising prices because the U.S. government cannot afford the high interest rates needed to control inflation. He blamed excessive government spending for the affordability crisis, warning that mounting fiscal pressures could trigger a broader economic collapse, potentially before the next presidential administration.
"We're now in the final stages of this collapse," he said, adding, "The whole thing can implode."
Economists Warn of AI-Driven Bubble Risks
Schiff had previously warned that rising borrowing costs could undermine AI investment and expose broader economic weakness. Former Fed adviser Danielle DiMartino Booth has similarly warned that a recession may already be underway, citing falling Treasury yields and mounting credit stress among AI companies. However, a prediction-market analysis showed only a 7% chance of a 2026 recession, although traders assigned greater recession risk to 2027.
Notably, the U.S. economy expanded at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, beating economists' 3.2% forecast and accelerating from 2.2% growth in the second quarter, according to the BEA's advance estimate.
NYU professor Scott Galloway warned that the AI infrastructure boom resembles the 1999 dot-com bubble, arguing that trillions of dollars in data-center and chip investments increasingly depend on demand from just two companies: OpenAI and Anthropic. He cautioned that this concentrated customer base could make the massive AI capital spending vulnerable.

item.title: Stocks decline on tech sell-off as concerns over the Nvidia fallout persist
item.author: CHAN HO-HIM
item.description:
Stocks decline on tech sell-off as concerns over the Nvidia fallout persist
2026-11-16
Por CHAN HO-HIM
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-decline-asia-investor-concerns-045636045.html
HONG KONG (AP) — World shares were mixed and Asian shares mostly declined Monday on another tech sell-off, as investors' worries over the future of the artificial intelligence trade extended into another week following Nvidia's fallout.
U.S. equity futures were lower. Investors and traders are closely monitoring any signals on what is next for the AI industry ahead of Nvidia's earnings report due Tuesday and Anthropic's massive stock market debut set for later this week.
In early European trading, Britain's FTSE 100 added 0.3% to 10,935.36. Germany's DAX was up less than 0.1% to 26,756.19, while France's CAC 40 rose 0.3% to 8,390.11.
Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO last week after his extramarital affair sparked U.S. national security concerns shook global markets. Huang has been one of the biggest advocates for AI and his downfall triggered questions over how the global AI boom could be impacted.
Those worries have spread to Asia, where AI hardware stocks are prominent on markets including in South Korea and Japan.
South Korea's benchmark Kospi index lost 3.6% to 5,100.50. Shares fell for memory chipmaker SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, two of its most valuable companies. SK Hynix plummeted 7.9%, while Samsung Electronics gave up 4.5%.
Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 2.4% to 59,662.02 after official data Monday showed Japan's economy contracted in the latest quarter. Several of Japan's big AI stock names also traded lower. OpenAI investor SoftBank Group slipped 3.7%, while memory maker Kioxia Holdings dropped 7.7% and chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron dipped 7.1%.
Also a beneficiary of the global AI frenzy, Taiwan's Taiex sank 6%, with shares of its leading chipmaker TSMC, or Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., falling 5.7%.
There have been increasing concerns that the robust growth of the AI capital spending may slow, analysts have said, even before the Nvidia episode. For one, uncertainties surrounding developments of AI data centers in the U.S. were also growing following the U.S. midterm elections.
"The market was already worried about this risk before what happened at Nvidia," Zhiwei Zhang, president and chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management said in a commentary Monday. "Now the risk has become even more serious."
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index rose 0.5% to 23,753.84. The Shanghai Composite index declined 0.9% to 3,602.57 following latest Chinese official economic data released Monday, including on retail sales and industrial production, that disappointed analysts.

item.title: Futuristic Shenzhen Shows Trump the Difficulty of Stopping China
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.description:
Futuristic Shenzhen Shows Trump the Difficulty of Stopping China
2026-11-16
Por Bloomberg News
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/futuristic-shenzhen-shows-trump-difficulty-230024603.html
(Bloomberg) -- Under the towering skyscrapers home to some of China's biggest tech giants, a small group of foreigners tilt up their smartphones to capture a drone descending from the Shenzhen sky with a fresh serving of bubble tea.
Most Read from Bloomberg
They've paid around $90 a head to be dazzled by the southern Chinese city's tech wonders on a tour led by Sean Zhang, who returned home in 2023 after studying in California. He's now cashing in as tourists flock to Shenzhen to experience frontier technologies like flying robotaxis, wearable exoskeletons and buildings shaped like giant AirPods. Influencers on Western social media platforms regularly post videos with titles like "China built a city that feels like 2050!"
"Shenzhen usually leaves a very good impression," says Zhang, 27, who has more than doubled the number of tours offered over the past year. "Many walk away saying: 'This isn't what I expected of China.'"
It's that innovation President Xi Jinping wants to show the world — and Donald Trump — when he hosts the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit this week in this city of some 18 million people. At the turn of the century, Shenzhen was best known for its cheap knock-offs of Western goods. Today, the city's progress serves as a powerful symbol of China's technological rise — and the limits of Washington's efforts to hold it back.
Dozens of companies in Shenzhen, including national tech champion Huawei Technologies Co. and Tencent Holdings Ltd., are on US blacklists designed to restrict their access to American exports and markets. But that hasn't stopped them going from strength to strength. BYD Co. last year dethroned US giant Tesla Inc. as the world's top supplier of electric vehicles, while SZ DJI Technology Co. now controls about 70% of the global consumer drone market.
That boom has made Shenzhen a bright spot even as it epitomizes the broader paradox in China's economy: While exports are surging and its tech companies are becoming global leaders, many locals aren't feeling any richer as wage growth slows and many firms struggle to eke out profits.
Shenzhen saw the highest population growth rate of any major Chinese city last year, and has one of the country's youngest average urban populations at 32.5 years old. Airport signs declare: "Once Here Shenzhener Forever." While China has a glut of unsold real estate — Goldman Sachs Group Inc. estimated in 2024 it would be worth $13 trillion if fully built — the city is actually seeing a supply squeeze, making it potentially the first place to climb out of the nation's five-year property slump.
"Shenzhen is no Potemkin showcase — its technological and industrial achievements are real," said Han Lin, China country director at The Asia Group, a Washington-based advisory firm. "But China has already demonstrated it can build world-class productive capacity. The harder challenge is generating sufficient domestic demand to absorb that capacity."
Shenzhen is among several megacities competing to be China's version of Silicon Valley. Beijing's top colleges produce some of the brightest AI researchers working at leading labs like DeepSeek and Moonshot AI. Shanghai and neighboring Hangzhou — home to Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. — are better known for fast-to-market AI applications for global markets.
Shenzhen stands out for its supply chains that help AI integrate into everyday life. One company emblematic of that strength is Seeed Studio, which focuses on "physical AI" — sensors, cameras and robot arms connecting AI to real-world tasks. Its studio displays warehouse interfaces, a chicken-farm system, panda conservation sensors and an AI-and-inventor van touring rural areas.

Dozens of companies in Shenzhen, including national tech champion Huawei Technologies Co. and Tencent Holdings Ltd., are on US blacklists designed to restrict their access to American exports and markets. But that hasn't stopped them going from strength to strength. BYD Co. last year dethroned US giant Tesla Inc. as the world's top supplier of electric vehicles, while SZ DJI Technology Co. now controls about 70% of the global consumer drone market.
That boom has made Shenzhen a bright spot even as it epitomizes the broader paradox in China's economy: While exports are surging and its tech companies are becoming global leaders, many locals aren't feeling any richer as wage growth slows and many firms struggle to eke out profits.
Shenzhen saw the highest population growth rate of any major Chinese city last year, and has one of the country's youngest average urban populations at 32.5 years old. Airport signs declare: "Once Here Shenzhener Forever." While China has a glut of unsold real estate — Goldman Sachs Group Inc. estimated in 2024 it would be worth $13 trillion if fully built — the city is actually seeing a supply squeeze, making it potentially the first place to climb out of the nation's five-year property slump.
"Shenzhen is no Potemkin showcase — its technological and industrial achievements are real," said Han Lin, China country director at The Asia Group, a Washington-based advisory firm. "But China has already demonstrated it can build world-class productive capacity. The harder challenge is generating sufficient domestic demand to absorb that capacity."
Shenzhen is among several megacities competing to be China's version of Silicon Valley. Beijing's top colleges produce some of the brightest AI researchers working at leading labs like DeepSeek and Moonshot AI. Shanghai and neighboring Hangzhou — home to Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. — are better known for fast-to-market AI applications for global markets.
Shenzhen stands out for its supply chains that help AI integrate into everyday life. One company emblematic of that strength is Seeed Studio, which focuses on "physical AI" — sensors, cameras and robot arms connecting AI to real-world tasks. Its studio displays warehouse interfaces, a chicken-farm system, panda conservation sensors and an AI-and-inventor van touring rural areas.

item.title: Haven't saved enough for retirement? Wealthy people haven't either.
item.author: Kerry Hannon
item.description:
Haven't saved enough for retirement? Wealthy people haven't either.
2026-11-16
Por Kerry Hannon
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/havent-saved-enough-for-retirement-wealthy-people-havent-either-192922069.html
The rich aren't that different from you and me.
They also agonize about having enough money set aside for retirement — even if the amount they need to "retire comfortably" is loftier.
Wealthy Americans say they will need $2.6 million to feel financially set to retire, up 26% from last year, according to a new study from financial services firm HSBC.
That savings target is roughly double the amount that less-wealthy workers aim for.
"For affluent households, it's not simply about accumulating a larger nest egg, but ensuring their wealth can sustain their desired lifestyle over several decades," Jessie Zhu, an HSBC managing director, told Yahoo Finance.
Savings lag behind
The problem is, wealthy savers are only halfway toward reaching their goal on average. Baby boomers, those nearest to retirement, have hit 74% of their target, while millennials clock in at just 42%.
That trend holds for those lower on the economic ladder, other surveys have found.
About half of workers surveyed by Schroders have less than $500,000 in savings at retirement — including 24% who say it's unlikely they will have $250,000 set aside.
Northwestern Mutual found that nearly half of workers it surveyed don't expect to be financially prepared and believe there's a good chance they'll outlive their savings.
Is delaying retirement a solution?
To help fill the coffers, nearly two-thirds of affluent Americans plan to stretch out their earnings years by slowly trimming back their working hours over time, the HSBC data found.
But formal phased retirement programs that offer a reduced or flexible schedule and a lighter workload have been few and far between. Last year, just 7% of firms surveyed by the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM) offered a formal program. A larger share—about 2 in 10— offered an informal arrangement in which workers create their own plan with their manager.
Like wealthier Americans, working longer is the fallback position for most of us. More than 4 in 10 workers expect to work past age 65 or do not plan to retire, according to Transamerica research.
But the harsh reality is that most people retire before they reach 65 due to a health issue, caregiving for an aging relative, or a job loss.
So how much should you be saving? It depends on many variables, including where you live, how expensive your lifestyle is, your health, and your financial obligations.
In general, you should aim to have 10 times your pre-retirement income saved by the time you reach age 67. If you have an annual salary of $100,000, that means $1 million saved by the time you retire.
Kerry Hannon is a Senior Columnist at Yahoo Finance. She is a career and retirement strategist and the author of 14 books, including "Retirement Bites: A Gen X Guide to Securing Your Financial Future," "In Control at 50+: How to Succeed in the New World of Work," and "Never Too Old to Get Rich.

item.title: What a Tiny Chorus of the ‘Bring Back Jensen’ Tech Bros Gets Wrong
item.author: Jeffrey Sonnenfeld; Stephen Henriques; Steven Tian; Bill George
item.description:
What a Tiny Chorus of the ‘Bring Back Jensen’ Tech Bros Gets Wrong
2026-11-16
Por Jeffrey Sonnenfeld; Stephen Henriques; Steven Tian; Bill George
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/tiny-chorus-bring-back-jensen-003000523.html
A small band of rogue tech bros has ridden to Jensen Huang's defense amidst a report from the Financial Times that Huang is huddling with allies, plotting a comeback as Nvidia CEO days after resigning, with a petition demanding "due process, not mob justice," signed by a minority of tech voices who have gotten outsized attention, such as Elon Musk and Atreides Management managing partner Gavin Baker. One tech bro even said, "Nvidia would be wrong to fire Jensen. His marital indiscretions are between him, his wife, and a reprimand from the board," as if that was all there is to the story.
But this small circle of rogue tech bros is wrong. This is not a story about a woke inquisition or prudes regulating marital indiscretions and sex – and a Sam Altman-style comeback does not make sense. We were supportive of Altman's comeback and knew Steve Jobs personally – and supported his firing and subsequent comeback. But these circumstances are materially different. There is no comeback here.
Start with the conduct the defenders wave away, of Huang's workplace affairs with direct subordinates. Huang admitted infidelity on Nov. 8. Days later, the New York Times reported a relationship with one of his direct reports. Nvidia's code of conduct, which opens with a letter from Huang himself, names "personal relationships" as a conflict of interest. We had firsthand knowledge of Mark Hurd's removal at HP over expense reports that concealed a personal relationship with a contractor, which was the right removal. Boards at McDonald's, Intel and Nestlé similarly removed CEOs over relationships with employees. Workplace romances with bosses having affairs with married direct reports put those subordinates in an inherently compromised position; they are deleterious to the morale of those around them, raising questions of merit and favoritism.
But when it comes to Huang and Nvidia's woes, workplace romance is the least of it. The relationship that should alarm Americans the most was Nvidia's "culture of noncompliance" on chip export restrictions to China, as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent put it on Sunday with Larry Kudlow, irrespective of whether or not Alice Huang, who helped set up Megaspeed, was an actual Chinese spy. As Bessent said, was Nvidia "pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?"
Evidence points to a fifth or more of Nvidia's compute revenue being tied to China
The paper trail when it comes to banned Nvidia chips illegally making their way into China at scale, evading U.S. restrictions, is particularly damning for the company.
Shipment records reviewed by the Wall Street Journal tie Megaspeed to nearly $12 billion in orders of Nvidia's most advanced chips for Chinese buyers between early 2024 and mid-2025, despite a balance sheet that showed a measly $33 million in 2023., according to Culper Research. Documents reviewed by Bloomberg show that a company Alice Huang founded told China's own central-bank credit registry that it held servers carrying banned H100, H200 and H800 chips in a Shanghai data center. Some were first sold to an official Nvidia cloud partner in Singapore and then subsequently laundered into China. In March, the Justice Department indicted Super Micro's co-founder, who has pleaded not guilty, for allegedly smuggling $2.5 billion of Nvidia-powered servers through a Southeast Asian front, with dummy servers staged for inspectors.
And where do such chips end up once they make their way into China? The Chinese Communist Party and the Chinese military, where they are used directly against the US.
Reuters found that Northwestern Polytechnical University, blacklisted by Washington since 2001 and one of China's "Seven Sons of National Defens
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO
item.author: Yahoo Finance
item.description:
Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO
2026-11-16
Por Yahoo Finance
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/article/anthropic-ipo-what-we-know-143321078.html
Subject to regulatory clearance, Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) will officially hold its initial public offering and set its pricing on Wednesday, Nov. 18, the company announced Thursday. It will begin trading under the ticker ANT on Thursday, Nov. 19.
The artificial intelligence startup publicly filed its S-1 paperwork for its initial public offering — the prospectus a company must file with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) before selling stock to the public — on Oct. 26, 2026.
Before Anthropic's stock can begin trading, the company's executives and its underwriters must complete an investor roadshow, set a price, and receive a final green light from regulators. The IPO roadshow started on November 10.
The countdown is on for one of the largest IPOs in history.
Anthropic IPO: What we know
- Date price will be set: Nov. 18, 2026
- Trading begins: Nov. 19, 2026.
- Stock ticker symbol: ANT
- Exchange: Nasdaq Global Select Market (Class A)
FAQS
When did the roadshow begin?
Anthropic said it began its roadshow on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The company is seeking a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion in its closely watched IPO.
Companies that let the SEC review a draft of their IPO paperwork in private are required to wait at least 15 calendar days after making it public before starting their formal roadshow — the meetings where bankers pitch the stock to big investors and take orders. Since Anthropic released its filing to the public on Oct. 26, Nov. 10 was the earliest possible date the roadshow could begin.
When will Anthropic set its IPO price?
Anthropic will set its IPO price on Nov. 18, 2026.
The maker of Claude disclosed on Tuesday in an updated filing that it will sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 each. The final price is usually set after investors have indicated their demand, the night before the stock starts trading.
On top of the public offering, Anthropic is locking down an extra $26 billion on the side from tech's biggest heavyweights, including Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), Google (GOOG, GOOGL), TSMC (TSM), Broadcom (AVGO), AMD (AMD), and Micron (MU). Those companies are buying non-voting Class N shares at the same price public investors will pay. Because this is a private deal, those tech giants won't face the standard six-month lockup window that typically prevents insiders from selling right after the debut.
What could change the schedule?
Many factors. Market volatility, particularly in comparable stocks already trading, and any outstanding regulatory issues could shift the timetable.
Should you buy Anthropic stock on day one?
History says patience pays off. Of more than 9,000 IPOs from 1975 to 2021, 60% were flat or lower three years after their first day's closing price, according to data from University of Florida professor Jay Ritter that Yahoo Finance analyzed before SpaceX's debut.
Anthropic could get the same early boost SpaceX (SPCX) did from index funds forced to buy the stock. But that buying may have come at a price for SpaceX, which fell 15% in its first week in the Nasdaq-100.
Who stands to make money from the IPO?
Early investors and institutions backing Anthropic may be in for a significant windfall. Anthropic's S-1 filing showed two of Anthropic's biggest backers — Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet — are likely to be winners.
Anthropic's venture capital backers, including Spark Capital, Menlo Ventures, Coatue Management, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, as well as funds managed by Fidelity and Blackstone, also stand to gain.
Some shareholders have already converted part of their holdings into cash ahead of the IPO. In April, Anthropic facilitated a tender offer in which shareholders, including CEO Dario Amodei, president Daniela Amodei, and other executives, sold approximatel
[Transcripcion recortada]

The maker of Claude disclosed on Tuesday in an updated filing that it will sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 each. The final price is usually set after investors have indicated their demand, the night before the stock starts trading.
On top of the public offering, Anthropic is locking down an extra $26 billion on the side from tech's biggest heavyweights, including Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), Google (GOOG, GOOGL), TSMC (TSM), Broadcom (AVGO), AMD (AMD), and Micron (MU). Those companies are buying non-voting Class N shares at the same price public investors will pay. Because this is a private deal, those tech giants won't face the standard six-month lockup window that typically prevents insiders from selling right after the debut.
What could change the schedule?
Many factors. Market volatility, particularly in comparable stocks already trading, and any outstanding regulatory issues could shift the timetable.
Should you buy Anthropic stock on day one?
History says patience pays off. Of more than 9,000 IPOs from 1975 to 2021, 60% were flat or lower three years after their first day's closing price, according to data from University of Florida professor Jay Ritter that Yahoo Finance analyzed before SpaceX's debut.
Anthropic could get the same early boost SpaceX (SPCX) did from index funds forced to buy the stock. But that buying may have come at a price for SpaceX, which fell 15% in its first week in the Nasdaq-100.
Who stands to make money from the IPO?
Early investors and institutions backing Anthropic may be in for a significant windfall. Anthropic's S-1 filing showed two of Anthropic's biggest backers — Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet — are likely to be winners.
Anthropic's venture capital backers, including Spark Capital, Menlo Ventures, Coatue Management, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, as well as funds managed by Fidelity and Blackstone, also stand to gain.
Some shareholders have already converted part of their holdings into cash ahead of the IPO. In April, Anthropic facilitated a tender offer in which shareholders, including CEO Dario Amodei, president Daniela Amodei, and other executives, sold approximatel

item.title: Rocket from Boeing-Lockheed firm fails mid-flight, destroys payload of Amazon satellites
item.author: Joey Roulette
item.description:
Rocket from Boeing-Lockheed firm fails mid-flight, destroys payload of Amazon satellites
2026-11-16
Por Joey Roulette
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-rocket-fails-launch-payload-202554696.html
By Joey Roulette
Nov 15 (Reuters) - A Vulcan rocket owned by United Launch Alliance, the joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed on Sunday shortly after liftoff from Florida, destroying its payload of 40 satellites from Amazon's Leo internet network in the launch company's first mission failure.
The rocket failed roughly 10 minutes after liftoff from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, and the cause was not immediately clear. It represented a major setback for the two-decade-old company's new flagship rocket as ULA sought to begin a regular cadence of launches for Amazon's burgeoning satellite internet constellation.
"Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in a statement.
"Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something. Since the anomaly just occurred, we don't have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today," ULA said.
The failure is expected to lead to a lengthy technical investigation that would keep the rocket off the market for months. This could deepen a US launch bottleneck brought on by other rocket mishaps and challenges across the industry as well as the looming retirement of SpaceX's Falcon 9, the world's most active rocket. SpaceX is no longer accepting bookings for the Falcon 9.
"There is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01," Amazon said in a statement, referring to the name of Sunday's mission. "ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they'll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan."
The Sunday flight was Vulcan's fifth since its 2024 debut and first in nine months, following a launch hiatus drawn out by separate technical investigations into its solid rocket side boosters and its core BE-4 engines, which are supplied by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin space company.
Blue Origin is working with ULA in the investigation into Sunday's failure, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.
The boosters were being scrutinized for issues encountered on Vulcan's last two flights, including a mission in February for the US Space Force. Both missions successfully delivered their payloads to orbit, but the Pentagon had not yet approved the rocket to resume flying national security payloads, pending its performance with the Amazon mission on Sunday.

item.title: Nvidia and Jensen Huang fallout: Here’s everything we know after a momentous week
item.author: Ethan Wolff-Mann
item.description:
Nvidia and Jensen Huang fallout: Here’s everything we know after a momentous week
2026-11-16
Por Ethan Wolff-Mann
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-and-jensen-huang-fallout-heres-everything-we-know-after-a-momentous-week-110000323.html
The rapid-fire pace of the Nvidia (NVDA) scandal has left everyone a little disoriented. So we thought we'd make a giant rundown of what's happened — and what we've been thinking about to help make sense of the very fluid situation.
Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned under pressure from the board. The one-two punch of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, and then news of another one with an Nvidia executive (plus a third with an unnamed employee revealed Thursday afternoon) turned out to be too much for the company's board to ignore. Huang was among the longest-serving CEOs in the S&P 500 (^GSPC), with a 33-year tenure.
What this means for earnings? Not much, beyond all the questions Kress will have to answer. That quarter is over. But all eyes will be on the outlook and on whether Nvidia seems to have its act together.
Context-wise, these are 2025 stock prices for NVDA. The stock is down 13% over the past five days, 25% in the past month (and the past six months), and 12% so far this year. And 14% from a year ago. The stock is essentially back to summer 2025 levels.
Wall Street is lowering price targets. Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives, a prominent Nvidia bull, lowered his price target from $300 to $225, valuing Huang's leadership at a 25% premium. The longer-term outlook, broadly, seems clouded, but most analyst notes we've read say that Kress's knowledge of the business makes her seem like a steady pair of hands.
The CEO search is going to be critical. Already, speculation about who will be the new permanent CEO has reached fever pitch, with President Trump suggesting Tim Cook, "the only one man to take his place."
Prediction markets favor Ian Buck as long-term successor. Kalshi and Polymarket are giving Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing a 1-in-3 chance. Here's who he is. Still, that's not a high probability, and it could be anyone with electrical engineering prowess or heavy Big Tech experience — preferably with charisma.
Another option being floated: ARM CEO Rene Haas.
What about the other co-founder? You may have noticed that Jensen Huang is Nvidia's "co-founder," not founder. The other one, Chris Malachowsky, is an engineer with tons of patents and "founder" cred who's also led Nvidia's research. He's another name to watch.
The House Foreign Affairs chair said Huang agreed to testify before Congress. Before Thanksgiving, and under oath, most likely. Huang can't retreat to a beach to escape the scandal anytime soon.
Democrats asked Nvidia to preserve all records.It's a clear indication that the China scandal is just getting started, despite Huang's departure.
Chinese AI is way cheaper for companies. Understanding why the Nvidia China scandal is important starts with the classic Chinese price advantage: doing things there is simply cheaper. Duolingo CEO Luis von Ahn told us this week that each AI interaction used to cost 30 cents and is now less than a cent, thanks to open-weight AI models, many of which are in China, like Alibaba's.

item.title: Rene Haas, Ian Buck, Chris Malachowsky: Wall Street zeroes in on potential Nvidia CEO successors
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Rene Haas, Ian Buck, Chris Malachowsky: Wall Street zeroes in on potential Nvidia CEO successors
2026-11-16
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/rene-haas-ian-buck-chris-malachowsky-wall-street-zeroes-in-on-potential-nvidia-ceo-successors-204105759.html
Wall Street is already speculating about who could take the permanent CEO role at Nvidia (NVDA) following Jensen Huang's abrupt departure, with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO.
Here's the list of names that have come up so far:
Rene Haas, Arm Holdings CEO
ARM (ARM) CEO Rene Haas is a potential successor to Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, according to the Financial Times.
Haas has been the leader of Arm since 2022. He became vice president and general manager of Nvidia's Computing Products Business Unit in October 2006 and left Nvidia for Arm in October 2013.
"He ran a business unit there and reported right into Jensen and knows him well," Patrick Moorhead, founder of Moor Insights and Strategy, told Yahoo Finance on Thursday.
"Rene has really done a great job in shepherding the company into where it is today," Unconventional AI CEO Naveen Rao said on Deirdre Bosa Live on Friday. "He's done great inside of Arm. I think Arm is a very different company from Nvidia."
"You need someone who really has that product vision, understands the technical details," Rao added.
Ian Buck, Nvidia vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing
Wall Street strategists have also floated Nvidia insider Ian Buck's name as the company's next leader. Prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket have zeroed in on the exec, with both sites ranking the odds of Buck taking over at roughly 40%.
Buck has worked at Nvidia for the last 22 years, rising from a systems engineer to his current role as the head of the company's biggest businesses.
The executive also has the kind of engineering chops that Nvidia's board may find compelling for the CEO role.
"He is the father of CUDA, and he runs the hyperscaler business at Nvidia, which is the lion's share of their revenue and profit dollars, and externally," Moorhead said.
Chris Malachowsky, Nvidia co-founder
Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky could also step in to serve as CEO. An accomplished engineer with nearly 40 patents to his name, Malachowsky is an Nvidia fellow and senior technology executive, according to a company biography,
Malachowsky has overseen efforts within Nvidia, including its operations and engineering. He's also led its research organization.
Tim Cook, former Apple CEO
Shortly after Nvidia's board announced Huang's immediate resignation, President Trump floated that former Apple (AAPL) CEO Tim Cook would be the best person for the top job at the AI chip giant.
"NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!" Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday.
On Friday, Polymarket bettors placed a 5% chance that Cook would be selected.
Yorkville's Dan Ives said Cook would be "a dark horse candidate in our view, given the global importance of Nvidia to the overall US tech industry."

item.title: Goldman Sachs sees upside for S&P 500 in 2027 — even as earnings growth slows
item.author: Paige Oamek
item.description:
Goldman Sachs sees upside for S&P 500 in 2027 — even as earnings growth slows
2026-11-16
Por Paige Oamek
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/goldman-sachs-sees-upside-for-sp-500-in-2027--even-as-earnings-growth-slows-185627269.html
Following a strong year for markets in 2026, Goldman Sachs strategists say they expect stocks to continue climbing next year despite slowing earnings growth.
In their 2027 global macro outlook, Goldman Sachs forecast the S&P 500 (^GSPC) to rise 14% from current levels to 8,700 next year. This year's gains were widespread, driven by surging company profits.
But while Goldman expects the stock market's profit boom to cool, spending on AI data centers to likely peak, and borrowing costs to remain high, the analysts noted that a recent sell-off in technology stocks has made valuations more attractive.
"Earnings growth is poised to slow," Peter Oppenheimer and his team wrote. "But equities have de-rated sharply; with more attractive valuations, positive but slower nominal economic and earnings growth, and lower bond yields, inflation and oil prices, we expect equities to continue to rise, but with high volatility."
As the bull market underpinned by artificial intelligence enters its fifth year, the Goldman team said slowing hyperscaler capex growth will "weaken the support for some of the 'picks and shovels' of the AI-related capex boom."
"Our economists expect a slowing in nominal GDP growth rates in 2027 as the AI investment boom peaks," the analysts wrote. "At the same time, nearly all markets are likely to see their earnings growth rates halve at least: in the US slowing from 36% to 11%."
Regionally, Goldman favors the US and Japan, stays neutral on Asia and emerging markets, and is cautious on Europe.
They also wrote that energy prices should moderate, predicting that Brent crude oil prices (BZ=F) will fall from around $100 per barrel at the end of 2026 to $78 per barrel at the end of 2027, bringing some commodity prices down with it.
"Combined with fading US tariff effects and easing AI-related supply pressures, this should lower inflation and help central banks bring it back towards target," Goldman's team wrote.
They recommend that investors look for companies that can sustain growth as growth becomes scarcer, selecting more stable, defensive picks such as healthcare and utilities.

Following a strong year for markets in 2026, Goldman Sachs strategists say they expect stocks to continue climbing next year despite slowing earnings growth.

In their 2027 global macro outlook, Goldman Sachs forecast the S&P 500 (^GSPC) to rise 14% from current levels to 8,700 next year. This year's gains were widespread, driven by surging company profits.

But while Goldman expects the stock market's profit boom to cool, spending on AI data centers to likely peak, and borrowing costs to remain high, the analysts noted that a recent sell-off in technology stocks has made valuations more attractive.

"Earnings growth is poised to slow," Peter Oppenheimer and his team wrote. "But equities have de-rated sharply; with more attractive valuations, positive but slower nominal economic and earnings growth, and lower bond yields, inflation and oil prices, we expect equities to continue to rise, but with high volatility."

As the bull market underpinned by artificial intelligence enters its fifth year, the Goldman team said slowing hyperscaler capex growth will "weaken the support for some of the 'picks and shovels' of the AI-related capex boom."

"Our economists expect a slowing in nominal GDP growth rates in 2027 as the AI investment boom peaks," the analysts wrote. "At the same time, nearly all markets are likely to see their earnings growth rates halve at least: in the US slowing from 36% to 11%."

Regionally, Goldman favors the US and Japan, stays neutral on Asia and emerging markets, and is cautious on Europe.

They also wrote that energy prices should moderate, predicting that Brent crude oil prices (BZ=F) will fall from around $100 per barrel at the end of 2026 to $78 per barrel at the end of 2027, bringing some commodity prices down with it.

"Combined with fading US tariff effects and easing AI-related supply pressures, this should lower inflation and help central banks bring it back towards target," Goldman's team wrote.

They recommend that investors look for companies that can sustain growth as growth becomes scarcer, selecting more stable, defensive picks such as healthcare and utilities.

item.title: Nvidia stock slips as Jensen Huang reportedly weighs CEO comeback, Musk backs return
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Nvidia stock slips as Jensen Huang reportedly weighs CEO comeback, Musk backs return
2026-11-16
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-stock-steady-as-jensen-huang-reportedly-weighs-ceo-comeback-musk-backs-return-015644730.html
Nvidia (NVDA) stock futures fell almost 2% on Monday as investors digested a report that supporters of Jensen Huang are lobbying for his return to the AI chip giant following his abrupt resignation last week.
Huang has discussed returning as CEO with confidants, the Financial Times reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Huang resigned last week following reports of affairs, including one with a woman who was reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy.
According to the report, a Huang supporter said that a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives was being assembled to lobby Nvidia's board to reinstate him, including by seeking support from the White House.
"Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that Huang supported the effort.
Meanwhile, SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk has come out in support of Huang, writing on X last Friday, "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen, and I'm signing it too."
On Saturday, Musk said, "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract. Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
The push to bring Huang back comes days after the FT reported that Nvidia's board had approached Arm Holdings (ARM) CEO Rene Haas as it searches for a successor. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO during the search.
Yorkville's Dan Ives said that while "no one individual can replace Jensen as CEO," any talk of "Jensen coming back to Nvidia is ridiculous in our view given the legal/Board/DC scrutiny/moral compass/China tentacles."
Huang abruptly stepped down Thursday following reports of alleged affairs with a former executive from Singapore-based Megaspeed, and also an Nvidia employee who reported directly to him.
Exactly one week earlier, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose how many affairs he had or identify those involved.
Recent reports have raised concerns about whether restricted semiconductors were being diverted to China and if sensitive US information had been sent to Beijing.
The developments have also sent shockwaves through the AI industry, where Nvidia has played a central role in building the ecosystem. The company has become a bellwether for the AI trade and has invested in key parts of the industry, including large language model development, energy, optics, and cloud providers.
Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results Tuesday after the bell, in what will be the company's first earnings call without Huang.
The stock declined more than 12% last week, closing below a $4 trillion market cap. At least 10 Wall Street analysts have downgraded the stock from Buy to Hold, with many citing, in part, increased scrutiny in Washington and succession uncertainty.
