item.title: 'Nothing has changed': Why some Nvidia stock bulls aren't wavering after Jensen Huang ouster
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
'Nothing has changed': Why some Nvidia stock bulls aren't wavering after Jensen Huang ouster
2026-11-16
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nothing-has-changed-why-some-nvidia-stock-bulls-arent-wavering-after-jensen-huang-ouster-204522204.html
Wall Street hasn't totally given up on Nvidia's (NVDA) stock. While there has been a steady stream of price targets this week and a few downgrades, a lot of analysts who cover the company are staying bullish.
Their argument is captured in one note from Wedbush analyst Matthew Bryson.
"Nothing has changed," Bryson wrote on Friday ahead of Nvidia's earnings next week.
"We again expect NVDA to exceed its forecast and to guide FQ4 above Street."
His rationale hinges on three points:
- "Management has tended to leave a fair bit [of] wiggle room in guidance, allowing for meaningful upside when reporting numbers and we expect NVDA will deliver another beat and raise quarter."
- "A strong hyperscaler spending backdrop augmented by increased spending at neoclouds and model builders (in particular xAI) is persisting into the out quarters as highlighted by results and guidance from Taiwan Semiconductor, AMD, SuperMicro, Foxconn, etc. as well as our own supply chain checks."
- "We believe NVDA has built a best in industry position with material and component suppliers through at least next year at a point where component and material access, not end demand, is defining shipments."
It has been a brutal week for the once-untouchable Nvidia founder Jensen Huang.
Huang was ousted as CEO of the company he founded in 1993 amid a shocking turn of events.
According to the New York Times, Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, one of Huang's 60 or so direct reports.
Reuters reported late Thursday that Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee. The employee's name was not released. Huang has been married to his wife Lori for more than 40 years.
While Nvidia looks for a successor, the board has installed longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
Interestingly, Nvidia's stock is only down 12% for the week. We say only because, at one point, not seeing Huang atop Nvidia would have been unthinkable, and given the leadership uncertainty, one would think the stock would be down a lot more.
"Questions about data center financing, politics, and most significantly, former CEO Jensen Huang's sudden resignation have seemingly sucked up the oxygen that had been fueling NVDA's momentum since the release of ChatGPT4.0," Bryson said.
Some oxygen is still being pumped into Nvidia's stock, it appears.

item.title: Virgen de El Buen Suceso
item.author: Desconocido
item.description:
Virgen de El Buen Suceso
2026-11-15
Por Desconocido
http://virgendeelbuensuceso.blogspot.com/2009/05/
Rosário de la Aurora 2017
Día 2 de febrero, a las 5:00 AM
En este año 2017 la Imagen Sagrada de La Virgen de El Buen Suceso fue trasladada desde su Trono Abacial en El Coro Alto del Monasterio al Retablo del Altar Mayor de su Iglesia el domingo día 22 de enero, por la tarde.
Podemos contemplarla y venerarla en estas dos fotos sacadas ese mismo día.
FECHAS IMPORTANTES PARA RECORDAR
16 de enero de 1635 – Muere la Venerable Sierva de Dios Madre Mariana de Jesús Torres, Fundadora del Monasterio y Confidente de la Virgen de El Buen Suceso.
17 de enero de 1577 – Fundación definitiva del Real Monasterio de la Limpia Concepción de la Ciudad de San Francisco de Quito, bajo el Patrocinio de Su Magestad el Rey de España Don Felipe II.
21 de enero de 1577 – Fenómeno milagroso con la Imagen de Nuestra Señora de La Paz en la Capilla del Monasterio de la Concepción de Quito, recién fundado. (Ver relato en esta misma página del Blog)
25 de enero de 1577 – Primeras Profesiones religiosas, de la Fundadoras, en el recién fundado Monasterio de la Concepción Franciscana de Quito.
Informaciones sobre el libro manuscrito la "Vida Admirable"
(…) unas revelaciones que se decían hechas por nuestra Señora del Buen Suceso a una santa monja española, miembro del monasterio de la Inmaculada Concepción en Quito. El nombre de aquella religiosa era Mariana de Jesús Torres, con respecto a la cual Monseñor Manuel María Pólit, el año 1903, emitió el juicio siguiente: [NOTA de los editores del Blog: este “juicio” fue escrito por Diego Rodríguez Docampo en su “Descripción del estado eclesiástico de San Francisco de Quito”, año 1650, publicada por Marcos Jiménez de la Espada en su colección de “Relaciones Geográficas de Indias”, en la Biblioteca de Autores Españoles, Tomo III, Madrid 1965, página 51. Es muy probable que Mons. Pólit las haya trascrito de alguna copia de esta Relación que conserven las monjas del Monasterio de Quito.]
"Santas ha habido y monjas de singular virtud y religión, como lo fueron Doña María Taboada, primera fundadora y Abadesa, y otras que imitaron su virtud. La que más resplandeció en humildad y obediencia, penitencia y don de oración, fue Mariana de Jesús, una de las primeras, y que desde niña tomó el hábito. Vivió y murió con grande ejemplo, así en lo espiritual y temporal como en su gobierno; siendo abadesa diversas veces; y cuyas súplicas y oraciones fueron aceptas a la Divina Majestad, pues se conseguía de su Misericordia lo que ella le pedía. Su muerte fue en tanta paz y santidad como en la que vivió. Sus confesores declararon, en los sermones que se hicieron en su entierro, honras y cabo de año, cómo fue muy celosa en el divino servicio, y que mereció grandes revelaciones de su Divina Majestad, y que tuvo don de profecía. Está recibida en esta opinión, y en la del Arzobispo-Obispo Ilmo. Dr. Don Fray Pedro de Oviedo, que la trató y confesó".
Nótese que Fray Pedro de Oviedo, que, a la sazón, era Obispo de Ouito, fue denominado Arzobispo, en razón de que tal dignidad había tenido antes, en la ciudad de Santo Domingo de la Isla Española. (8) -- (NOTA 8) El juicio de Monseñor Pólit, en el semanario quiteño "El Amigo", 4 de diciembre de 1943. - Consta en la Historia del Ecuador, tomo 4º, páginas 205 y siguientes, escrita por Monseñor Federico González Suárez, que Fray Pedro de Oviedo fue obispo de Quito en esos años.
Pues bien, la vida y revelaciones de Sor Mariana de Jesús Torres fueron descritas en tiempo aún de la colonia, por la pluma de un religioso franciscano portugués, Manuel Sousa Pereira, por el año 1792. Resultado: tres cuadernos manuscritos, los cuales, habiendo estado por el espacio de muchos lustros en el monasterio de la Concepción, finalmente vinieron a parar en manos del Presidente García Moreno, entregados por la Abadesa, Sor Bárbara Fierro, nativa de Tulcán. (9 y 10) -- (NOTA 9) Por declaración de las m
[Transcripcion recortada]

Rosário de la Aurora 2017
Día 2 de febrero, a las 5:00 AM
En este año 2017 la Imagen Sagrada de La Virgen de El Buen Suceso fue trasladada desde su Trono Abacial en El Coro Alto del Monasterio al Retablo del Altar Mayor de su Iglesia el domingo día 22 de enero, por la tarde.
Podemos contemplarla y venerarla en estas dos fotos sacadas ese mismo día.
FECHAS IMPORTANTES PARA RECORDAR
16 de enero de 1635 – Muere la Venerable Sierva de Dios Madre Mariana de Jesús Torres, Fundadora del Monasterio y Confidente de la Virgen de El Buen Suceso.
17 de enero de 1577 – Fundación definitiva del Real Monasterio de la Limpia Concepción de la Ciudad de San Francisco de Quito, bajo el Patrocinio de Su Magestad el Rey de España Don Felipe II.
21 de enero de 1577 – Fenómeno milagroso con la Imagen de Nuestra Señora de La Paz en la Capilla del Monasterio de la Concepción de Quito, recién fundado. (Ver relato en esta misma página del Blog)
25 de enero de 1577 – Primeras Profesiones religiosas, de la Fundadoras, en el recién fundado Monasterio de la Concepción Franciscana de Quito.
Informaciones sobre el libro manuscrito la "Vida Admirable"
(…) unas revelaciones que se decían hechas por nuestra Señora del Buen Suceso a una santa monja española, miembro del monasterio de la Inmaculada Concepción en Quito. El nombre de aquella religiosa era Mariana de Jesús Torres, con respecto a la cual Monseñor Manuel María Pólit, el año 1903, emitió el juicio siguiente: [NOTA de los editores del Blog: este “juicio” fue escrito por Diego Rodríguez Docampo en su “Descripción del estado eclesiástico de San Francisco de Quito”, año 1650, publicada por Marcos Jiménez de la Espada en su colección de “Relaciones Geográficas de Indias”, en la Biblioteca de Autores Españoles, Tomo III, Madrid 1965, página 51. Es muy probable que Mons. Pólit las haya trascrito de alguna copia de esta Relación que conserven las monjas del Monasterio de Quito.]
"Santas ha habido y monjas de singular virtud y religión, como lo fueron Doña María Taboada, primera fundadora y Abadesa, y otras que imitaron su virtud. La que más resplandeció en humildad y obediencia, penitencia y don de oración, fue Mariana de Jesús, una de las primeras, y que desde niña tomó el hábito. Vivió y murió con grande ejemplo, así en lo espiritual y temporal como en su gobierno; siendo abadesa diversas veces; y cuyas súplicas y oraciones fueron aceptas a la Divina Majestad, pues se conseguía de su Misericordia lo que ella le pedía. Su muerte fue en tanta paz y santidad como en la que vivió. Sus confesores declararon, en los sermones que se hicieron en su entierro, honras y cabo de año, cómo fue muy celosa en el divino servicio, y que mereció grandes revelaciones de su Divina Majestad, y que tuvo don de profecía. Está recibida en esta opinión, y en la del Arzobispo-Obispo Ilmo. Dr. Don Fray Pedro de Oviedo, que la trató y confesó".
Nótese que Fray Pedro de Oviedo, que, a la sazón, era Obispo de Ouito, fue denominado Arzobispo, en razón de que tal dignidad había tenido antes, en la ciudad de Santo Domingo de la Isla Española. (8) -- (NOTA 8) El juicio de Monseñor Pólit, en el semanario quiteño "El Amigo", 4 de diciembre de 1943. - Consta en la Historia del Ecuador, tomo 4º, páginas 205 y siguientes, escrita por Monseñor Federico González Suárez, que Fray Pedro de Oviedo fue obispo de Quito en esos años.
Pues bien, la vida y revelaciones de Sor Mariana de Jesús Torres fueron descritas en tiempo aún de la colonia, por la pluma de un religioso franciscano portugués, Manuel Sousa Pereira, por el año 1792. item.title: 3 signs AI stocks may be a great trade again
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
3 signs AI stocks may be a great trade again
2026-11-14
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/3-signs-ai-stocks-may-be-a-great-trade-again-130410381.html
Many AI stock bulls may be mourning the loss of Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia (NVDA), but they shouldn't sulk for too long.
The AI trade may be back, for now, after an early fall slumber. Here are several under-the-radar moves in the AI sector this week that investors may have overlooked amid the outsized focus on the Huang scandals.
Cisco's strong guidance
If AI demand is beginning to slow, you didn't see it in the quarter or outlook from networking giant Cisco (CSCO) late Thursday.
The company beat on the top and bottom lines for the most recent quarter. Guidance for the current quarter was also above estimates.
Cisco raised its expectation for AI infrastructure sales from hyperscalers to $9 billion this fiscal year. That would be more than double the results from the previous fiscal year.
"We're executing against our strategy and seeing growing demand as customers invest in the infrastructure they need for the AI or SI era," Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins said.
KeyBanc analyst Brandon Nispel said the stock looks "attractively" valued in the wake of earnings.
Cerebras mirrors Cisco
The AI infrastructure play, similar to Cisco, beat on sales and earnings in the most recent quarter late Thursday.
Cerebras (CBRS) said it sees a core gross margin of 47% to 49% and sales of $310 million to $330 million for the current quarter. Analysts had estimated a 42.1% gross margin and $271 million in sales.
"Net-net, key customers remain intact, CBRS is adding new hyperscalers, but the industry is experiencing LPS delays across many providers, which is causing slowness in the OAI ramp and could push timing of revenue," Barclays analyst Tom O'Malley said. "With the level of pressure the company saw over the last month (-33% vs. SOX -14%), we think the clearing of the bear case and new customers should more than offset industry-wide concerns on LPS delays in the near term. The new focus should be on execution of OAI and the new customer set."
Shares surged 13% in premarket trading on Friday.
CoreWeave calms the bears
CoreWeave (CRWV) left nothing for the bears to chew on when it reported earnings earlier this week.
The company beat on the top and bottom lines. It signaled strong demand trends. And it fought back against the view that it would need to tap high-yield debt markets to fuel its growth.
"We already have a robust pipeline of customers competing for this capacity. At current pricing levels, 2027 renewals would generate approaching $4 billion of incremental annualized revenue with no additional capex required," CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said. "This grows to nearly $10 billion of annualized incremental revenue when including 2028 renewals. Furthermore, if data center construction across the sector were to slow, installed compute becomes scarcer, and the knock-on effect is that GPU pricing may stay higher for longer."
Shares of CoreWeave are up 22% this week.

item.title: Fed’s Collins Says Inflation Fight Outweighs Housing Woes
item.author: Maria Eloisa Capurro
item.description:
Fed’s Collins Says Inflation Fight Outweighs Housing Woes
2026-11-14
Por Maria Eloisa Capurro
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/fed-collins-says-inflation-fight-141000214.html
(Bloomberg) -- Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins signaled Friday that tighter monetary policy may be needed to cool prices.
Most Read from Bloomberg
In a speech centered on the housing market, Collins said higher interest rates can limit housing affordability. Still, she added, ensuring price stability will benefit both the housing market and the overall economy in the long run.
"In the near term, the higher interest rates sometimes needed to cool the economy and keep inflation in check can make homes more expensive to buy and to build," Collins said in remarks prepared for the Boston Fed's annual economic conference. "But over the longer run, stable prices create predictable economic conditions that are good for housing."
After tightening monetary policy for the first time in three years in September, Fed officials held their benchmark rate steady last month. Several policymakers have signaled their support for a rate increase in December following hotter-than-expected inflation data for October. Investors currently anticipate hikes in December and January, with a third in either March or April, based on federal funds futures pricing.

item.title: Bill Ackman calls Anthropic 'the most amazing business story of this century' — but he's not a buyer
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Bill Ackman calls Anthropic 'the most amazing business story of this century' — but he's not a buyer
2026-11-14
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bill-ackman-calls-anthropic-the-most-amazing-business-story-of-this-century--but-hes-not-a-buyer-212201323.html
Bill Ackman calls Anthropic 'the most amazing business story of this century' — but he's not a buyer
Pershing Square Capital CEO Bill Ackman thinks Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) is a great story with a business that has real potential. Just don't expect him to be a buyer early on when Anthropic becomes publicly traded.
"We think of ourselves as very low-risk investors. We want to invest in businesses that we can predict with a very high degree of confidence," the well-known value investor said at Yahoo Finance Invest. "I think Anthropic is perhaps the most amazing business story of this century in terms of from zero to where it is today — it's an absolutely remarkable story. An incredibly impressive story. I think it's just a much more complicated question as to what that business is worth. It's very hard to nail that with any degree of precision. It could be worth a lot more, a lot less, depending upon a few variables that are difficult to predict. And that's why it doesn't fit into our portfolio."
Anthropic has set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share, targeting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion. The company could raise up to $100 billion from its IPO at the high end of the range.
Read more: Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO
But the business has a lot to prove to justify keeping such a lofty valuation in public markets.
In an amended S-1 filing, Anthropic said that third quarter sales rose 1,127% to $17 billion. Revenue growth slowed on a quarter-over-quarter basis. Third quarter sales increased 47% compared with a 144% growth rate in the second quarter. Sales increased 132% in the first quarter.
The company also lost a staggering $23.29 billion in the third quarter.
Anthropic is expected to debut on public markets on Thursday, Nov. 19. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.
"I think Anthropic is on the cusp, or might even be at, a place in terms of its operating profitability, where it's real operating profitability," Ackman added. "I think the issue is if Anthropic doesn't stay in the lead position, then the real questions about the business model [emerge]. So the capex they have to spend is really real … So I would just say it's a much more complicated question. And there's a much wider range of outcomes — it's a more speculative bet than buying, for example, Visa, a company we own."

item.title: ‘I’m a Piece of Sh--’: Jensen Huang’s Last Hours as Nvidia CEO
item.author: Drake Bennett; Ian King
item.description:
‘I’m a Piece of Sh--’: Jensen Huang’s Last Hours as Nvidia CEO
2026-11-14
Por Drake Bennett; Ian King
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/m-piece-sh-jensen-huang-005649526.html
(Bloomberg) -- At the end, Jensen Huang looked broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted. After weeks spent denying the allegations of infidelity and fighting to remain in his job as Nvidia Corp.'s chief executive officer, his surrender late Wednesday night was unconditional. Huang's usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and he'd started using phrases like "whatever" and "I don't care."
For the decades he spent building Nvidia into a multitrillion-dollar AI chip behemoth, Huang was famous for his attention to the tiniest of details, from chip architecture to the compensation packages of even the most junior employees at the company. Now, in the eyes of the people in the room, he had given up.
It was a stunningly quick fall for a billionaire and tech titan who two weeks ago was the face of artificial intelligence around the world. With his directness and vigor, he had charmed US President Donald Trump, shaped global tech policy and drawn adoring crowds on his papal-style international tours.
It's hard to imagine the current AI boom happening without Huang, his company and their chips, and it's hard to imagine what it will look like after his fall. As Harvey Jones, chair of the company's board of directors, wrote in an email to employees after Huang's ouster, "Jensen's contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world."
Huang couldn't be reached for comment.
When the news broke in late October that Huang had close ties with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, it looked like he would prevail. The board of directors, dominated by longtime investors, business partners and friends of Huang's, was reluctant to act on the news stories, or even publicly comment on them.
Most of the news coverage tiptoed around the exact nature of the CEO's relationship with Alice Huang, the suspected spy. Huang denied to friends and colleagues that he had been unfaithful to his wife. He'd been denying it when questioned internally since late 2025. In one of his last interviews as CEO, Huang told Bloomberg News that his relationship with Alice Huang was typical of those with Chinese customers and executives. "It was all completely normal and not unusual," he said.
A turning point came last Friday, Nov. 6, when a Financial Times story cited US officials saying that the relationship had been a romantic one. Soon afterward, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter went to Huang's house to confront him, and Huang confessed. At that point, most of the board still didn't want to take a public stance, but Teter, who is secretary of the board, told them they had to act. The next day, Saturday, the board announced that they would investigate the allegations. A prominent law firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, would lead the inquiry. On Sunday, Huang emailed the entire company, admitting to the affair, apologizing to his family and vowing to "cooperate fully" with the board's investigation.
As the scandal ballooned, there was evidence that it was, perhaps unsurprisingly, drawing Huang's attention away from his extensive duties at the company. As part of Nvidia's idiosyncratic org chart, Huang had around 60 executives at the company who reported to him, a small army by normal management standards. The whole company had to file emails with their top five priorities, which Huang used to check that everyone was working on what he considered most important. Normally he responded to them immediately at all hours of the day and night. In recent days the response times had grown longer.
On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang was also having an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. Th
[Transcripcion recortada]

For the decades he spent building Nvidia into a multitrillion-dollar AI chip behemoth, Huang was famous for his attention to the tiniest of details, from chip architecture to the compensation packages of even the most junior employees at the company. Now, in the eyes of the people in the room, he had given up.

It was a stunningly quick fall for a billionaire and tech titan who two weeks ago was the face of artificial intelligence around the world. With his directness and vigor, he had charmed US President Donald Trump, shaped global tech policy and drawn adoring crowds on his papal-style international tours.

It's hard to imagine the current AI boom happening without Huang, his company and their chips, and it's hard to imagine what it will look like after his fall. As Harvey Jones, chair of the company's board of directors, wrote in an email to employees after Huang's ouster, "Jensen's contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world."

Huang couldn't be reached for comment.

When the news broke in late October that Huang had close ties with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, it looked like he would prevail. The board of directors, dominated by longtime investors, business partners and friends of Huang's, was reluctant to act on the news stories, or even publicly comment on them.

Most of the news coverage tiptoed around the exact nature of the CEO's relationship with Alice Huang, the suspected spy. Huang denied to friends and colleagues that he had been unfaithful to his wife. He'd been denying it when questioned internally since late 2025. In one of his last interviews as CEO, Huang told Bloomberg News that his relationship with Alice Huang was typical of those with Chinese customers and executives. "It was all completely normal and not unusual," he said.

A turning point came last Friday, Nov. 6, when a Financial Times story cited US officials saying that the relationship had been a romantic one. Soon afterward, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter went to Huang's house to confront him, and Huang confessed. At that point, most of the board still didn't want to take a public stance, but Teter, who is secretary of the board, told them they had to act. The next day, Saturday, the board announced that they would investigate the allegations. A prominent law firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, would lead the inquiry. On Sunday, Huang emailed the entire company, admitting to the affair, apologizing to his family and vowing to "cooperate fully" with the board's investigation.

As the scandal ballooned, there was evidence that it was, perhaps unsurprisingly, drawing Huang's attention away from his extensive duties at the company. As part of Nvidia's idiosyncratic org chart, Huang had around 60 executives at the company who reported to him, a small army by normal management standards. The whole company had to file emails with their top five priorities, which Huang used to check that everyone was working on what he considered most important. Normally he responded to them immediately at all hours of the day and night. In recent days the response times had grown longer.

On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang was also having an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. Th

item.title: The bull market in stocks is being put to the test. 2027 may not be any easier.
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
The bull market in stocks is being put to the test. 2027 may not be any easier.
2026-11-14
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-bull-market-in-stocks-is-being-put-to-the-test-2027-may-not-be-any-easier-134713002.html
The bull market won't have it easy in 2027 as the vibes around AI investments weaken, Goldman Sachs warned.
"Although we expect solid AI investment growth to continue, our forecasts imply that the investment growth impulse — additional AI investment as a share of GDP — will peak in early 2027. From a macro perspective, this should be a manageable event. But it may be a bigger test for markets for three reasons," Goldman Sachs strategist Kamakshya Trivedi said.
"First, the AI impulse has been a much larger contributor to growth in earnings and market value than to growth in GDP," Trivedi explained.
"Second, AI-related equities have taken credit for significant macro productivity gains, especially companies benefiting directly from the infrastructure boom, that have made them more vulnerable to any signs that we are on a less optimistic path," Trivedi added.
Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility
"Third, the point at which growth rates peak (a "second derivative" turning point) often matters, even if underlying growth rates (the "first derivative") remain healthy. Moving through that peak allows markets to place limits on the upside of an uncertain distribution and, as growth decelerates, the period of positive surprises to expectations often ends too, as we may be starting to see for the AI capex cycle."
Stocks have already been put to the test entering the final weeks of the year.
Market volatility has spiked in recent weeks amid the midterm election aftermath, which will see Democrats take control of the House and Senate in 2027.
High-stakes earnings reports from hyperscalers like Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) freaked out the market as they highlighted dwindling free cash flow.
The removal of Jensen Huang as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO has also triggered a sharp sell-off in hot sectors.
At the same time, macro headwinds have intensified as crude oil prices remain elevated amid geopolitical friction in the Middle East, reigniting fears of sticky headline inflation.
Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee said at Yahoo Finance Invest that he thinks the inflation problem is disturbing.
Trivedi added, "AI has contributed more to market gains than economic growth, so [it] is a bigger test for markets than the economy."

item.title: Goldman Sees S&P 500 Rising 14% on Cheap Hyperscaler Valuations
item.author: Julien Ponthus
item.description:
Goldman Sees S&P 500 Rising 14% on Cheap Hyperscaler Valuations
2026-11-14
Por Julien Ponthus
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/goldman-sees-p-500-rising-101415506.html
(Bloomberg) -- Goldman Sachs Group Inc. strategists are bullish on US stocks for 2027, predicting the S&P 500 will advance 14% over the coming year after a selloff in the biggest technology companies left their valuations historically cheap.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The team led by Peter Oppenheimer are overweight on the US and Japan for next year. They said in a note to clients that they see the S&P 500 hitting 8,700 points in the next 12 months, even as they expect earnings growth for the benchmark to slow sharply. The S&P is up 11% so far in 2026.
Goldman's call comes after the Nasdaq 100 dropped 9% from its early October high, dragged down by concerns over the artificial-intelligence buildout and the scandal at Nvidia Corp. that cost Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang his job this week. The declines have left so-called hyperscalers trading "well below" their historical valuations, the strategists said.
"We see Technology — and the Hyperscalers in particular — as relatively defensive," they wrote. "True, the biggest companies have turned cash flow negative, but overall balance sheet measures such as net debt/equity remain healthy."
With global earnings growth expected to ease in 2027, the team recommended investing in US and Japanese stocks and in industries that typically thrive amid lower bond yields, easing inflation and falling oil prices. They forecast a rapid deceleration in earnings-per-share expansion, with EPS growth on the S&P 500 sliding to 11% next year from 36% in 2026, and to 7% from 18% for the Stoxx Europe 600.
That, in turn, means markets are likely to assign a premium to the companies that continue expanding rapidly, according to Goldman.
"We expect investors to seek companies that can sustain growth as it becomes more scarce," the Goldman strategists wrote. "Attractive opportunities are emerging in long-duration growth companies, which should become more valuable as growth rates slow."
The bank is underweight European stocks, with Oppenheimer's team arguing valuations haven't come off as much as in other regions, while government debt "issues" and "a heavy political calendar" mean risks are higher. The Stoxx Europe 600 hit a fresh record this week, boosted by an upbeat earnings season and investors rotating out of the AI trade.

item.title: Nvidia’s Chris Malachowsky cofounded the company and is seen as a potential successor to Huang
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia’s Chris Malachowsky cofounded the company and is seen as a potential successor to Huang
2026-11-14
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-co-founder-chris-malachowsky-is-seen-as-a-potential-successor-to-huang-181629983.html
With Jensen Huang out as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO following his affair scandals, CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO.
The company's board is now searching both internally and externally for a permanent replacement for Huang.
Rene Haas, the CEO of Arm Holdings, is a contender, and Ian Buck, Nvidia's head of hyperscale and high-performance computing, is considered an early frontrunner for the position thanks to his strong technical expertise.
Buck created the CUDA software that enables developers to use Nvidia's chips for general-purpose computing, helping turn the company into the AI juggernaut it is today.
Buck isn't the only candidate, however.
Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky could also step in to serve as CEO.
An accomplished engineer with nearly 40 patents to his name, Malachowsky is an Nvidia fellow and senior technology executive, a biography on the company's site states.
Malachowsky has overseen efforts within Nvidia, including its operations and engineering. He's also led its research organization.
But whether Malachowsky, or anyone, for that matter, can fully replace Huang remains to be seen. The former CEO was Nvidia's biggest champion and the face of the AI era.
He hosted enormous keynote events, clad in his signature leather jackets, and traveled the world, drawing massive crowds as an AI ambassador.
He also had the kind of deep connections necessary to attract customers and make investments in a variety of AI-related businesses.
For now, Kress will serve as a steadying force within Nvidia as it seeks to find its footing following the past week's drama.
But the company's board will have to make a decision sooner or later, and whoever it chooses will determine the future of one of the world's most important companies. Sounds easy.

item.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei aims to 'underpromise and overdeliver' as IPO valuation drops below $2T hopes
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei aims to 'underpromise and overdeliver' as IPO valuation drops below $2T hopes
2026-11-14
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropic-ceo-dario-amodei-aims-to-underpromise-and-overdeliver-as-ipo-valuation-drops-below-2t-hopes-181234804.html
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei aims to 'underpromise and overdeliver' as IPO valuation drops below $2T hopes
A future of new scientific discovery where cancer, Alzheimer's, and heart disease are considered relics of the past, and artificial intelligence agents perform a growing number of complex tasks for humans safely.
Those were among the ambitions Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) CEO Dario Amodei laid out to JPMorgan Chase (JPM) CEO Jamie Dimon Friday as the artificial intelligence startup prepares for one of the largest initial public offerings in history.
"We can have a much more beautiful world… It sounds starry-eyed. It sounds crazy. I really do believe it," Amodei said.
The remarks came during a livestreamed conversation hosted at JPMorgan's Manhattan headquarters, one of Anthropic's final stops this week in its Wall Street push to drum up investor demand for its IPO next week.
Amodei laid out a sweeping vision for the technology, from accelerating scientific discoveries and transforming medicine to deploying increasingly capable AI agents in fields such as robotics and cybersecurity.
He also pointed to the company's technology creating new markets.
"You're on an exponential of cognition, and as the exponential proceeds, new markets become possible," Amodei told Dimon.
But realizing those ambitions comes with enormous financial costs. Amodei described securing enough computing power to support Anthropic's growth without spending beyond its means as the company's "deepest business dilemma."
Asked by Dimon why Anthropic is going public now, the Princeton PhD pointed to the need for additional cash to help manage the uncertainty surrounding Anthropic's computing investments.
The company must commit to expensive infrastructure well before it knows how much demand its AI products will generate. Amodei said Anthropic generally purchases less capacity in advance than its growth projections might justify, supplementing it when demand exceeds expectations.
"We actually tend to buy on the low side," he said.
The IPO would provide an additional financial cushion as Anthropic balances those risks against its extraordinary growth ambitions.
"Just the more cash we have on hand, the more buffer we have between those two things," Amodei said, while suggesting the company isn't seeking to secure its highest valuation possible.
Anthropic wants to "underpromise and overdeliver," Amodei said.
Anthropic expects to price its offering Wednesday and begin trading Thursday, Nov. 19, seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion through its IPO and a concurrent private share sale at a valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion, according to the company's IPO website.

"We can have a much more beautiful world… It sounds starry-eyed. It sounds crazy. I really do believe it," Amodei said.

The remarks came during a livestreamed conversation hosted at JPMorgan's Manhattan headquarters, one of Anthropic's final stops this week in its Wall Street push to drum up investor demand for its IPO next week.

Amodei laid out a sweeping vision for the technology, from accelerating scientific discoveries and transforming medicine to deploying increasingly capable AI agents in fields such as robotics and cybersecurity.

He also pointed to the company's technology creating new markets.

"You're on an exponential of cognition, and as the exponential proceeds, new markets become possible," Amodei told Dimon.

But realizing those ambitions comes with enormous financial costs. Amodei described securing enough computing power to support Anthropic's growth without spending beyond its means as the company's "deepest business dilemma."

Asked by Dimon why Anthropic is going public now, the Princeton PhD pointed to the need for additional cash to help manage the uncertainty surrounding Anthropic's computing investments.

The company must commit to expensive infrastructure well before it knows how much demand its AI products will generate. Amodei said Anthropic generally purchases less capacity in advance than its growth projections might justify, supplementing it when demand exceeds expectations.

"We actually tend to buy on the low side," he said.

The IPO would provide an additional financial cushion as Anthropic balances those risks against its extraordinary growth ambitions.

"Just the more cash we have on hand, the more buffer we have between those two things," Amodei said, while suggesting the company isn't seeking to secure its highest valuation possible.

Anthropic wants to "underpromise and overdeliver," Amodei said.

Anthropic expects to price its offering Wednesday and begin trading Thursday, Nov. 19, seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion through its IPO and a concurrent private share sale at a valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion, according to the company's IPO website.

item.title: ‘An intergalactic freak show’: Republicans are piling on Howard Lutnick
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
‘An intergalactic freak show’: Republicans are piling on Howard Lutnick
2026-11-14
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/lutnick-agrees-to-testify-before-congress-as-republicans-pile-on-the-embattled-commerce-secretary-151715681.html
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has reportedly agreed to testify before lawmakers next month as the spotlight on him grows harsher amid Nvidia's (NVDA) turmoil.
Both Democrats and Republicans alike are raising questions about whether Lutnick went too far in protecting Nvidia's push to sell its chips overseas even as the US government was warning about a possible security breach.
Lutnick is reportedly set to appear on Dec. 10 before the Senate Banking Committee, in news first reported by Fox News. Spokespersons for the Commerce Department and the Senate panel did not immediately provide additional details.
The appearance would set up what could be a major moment for the suddenly embattled Commerce secretary after days in which he and the White House had largely stayed silent as even some of Trump's closest allies grew more vocal.
Lutnick will appear before Republican Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the Senate panel until the end of the year and a regular on President Trump's campaign stops last month. Scott released a letter Thursday evening requesting that Lutnick and ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang appear before Congress early next month.
"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology," Scott wrote. "The American people deserve answers."
Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana used more colorful language in a recent appearance on CNN, saying he wanted answers about why the Commerce Department allowed Nvidia to sell chips to an alleged Chinese spy's company.
"This whole thing is an intergalactic freak show," Kennedy said.
Some Trump aides have declined to defend Lutnick emphatically.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent raised eyebrows Friday during a CNBC appearance when he reiterated his desire for stronger government limits on advanced semiconductor exports — which he added that the Pentagon, State Department, and the trade representative's office agreed with.
"Commerce has the pen…," Bessent said, "and you will have to ask them about their internal processes."
The rapid-fire developments have also increased the odds of Congress passing new curbs on semiconductor exports to China, with lawmakers now moving to add some combination of three bipartisan plans into a military funding bill that needs to pass before the end of the year.
A White House official said that Trump maintains confidence in Lutnick, but the president's only direct reaction to the scandal in recent days was a Truth Social post saying Huang had "done a fantastic job" and that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over Nvidia.

item.title: PPI report: Inflation shows signs of broadening in red-hot wholesale prices, keeping pressure on Fed to hike rates
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
PPI report: Inflation shows signs of broadening in red-hot wholesale prices, keeping pressure on Fed to hike rates
2026-11-14
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/ppi-report-inflation-shows-signs-of-broadening-in-red-hot-wholesale-prices-keeping-pressure-on-fed-to-hike-rates-162115609.html
PPI report: Inflation shows signs of broadening in red-hot wholesale prices, keeping pressure on Fed to hike rates
US wholesale prices surged to a four-year high in October as broad, sticky inflation across manufacturing and supply chains reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates by 25 basis points next month.
The Producer Price Index for final demand, which measures the prices that factories, farmers, and producers charge for their finished goods and services, rose 6.5% last month, the largest increase since the aftermath of the pandemic when prices jumped 7.4% in 2022. Expectations were for the wholesale price index to rise 6.6%.
On a core basis, excluding food, energy, and trade services, PPI rose 4.9% in October, compared with 5% in September, indicating that wholesale cost pressures persisted beyond the energy sector into other segments of the economy.
Read more: What is inflation, and how does it affect you?
Fed officials are noticing.
Boston Fed president Susan Collins told Bloomberg TV Friday morning that she hadn't had a chance to do a deep dive on the PPI data, but that after receiving CPI data along with the wholesale price data that "we're actually seeing some broadening evidence of broadening of price pressures" and "it's clear the direction and the numbers are less promising than, you know, I might have hoped."
"It's clear the direction that monetary policy needs to go, and I would think that soon some additional firming tightening of policy is appropriate," she said.
Collins also said of the path for rates that "it may be that a bit of a tighter policy path than I had penciled in a couple of months ago might be appropriate, but I think how high and how quickly is something we're going to have to decide meeting by meeting."
Fed governor Michelle Bowman said Tuesday that with inflation showing signs of broadening, rate hikes may be needed to slow the pace of price increases.
"Inflation pressures have persisted for longer than I had hoped and have shown recent signs of broadening," Bowman said in a speech in Washington.
Hawkish stance from the Fed
Meanwhile, in the PPI report, a surge in transportation and warehousing prices underscored that higher diesel prices were still showing up.
This marked the second month in a row of exceptionally high wholesale prices, following a more than 6% rise in September.
Over 60% of the total price increase for physical goods came from everyday manufactured products, rather than from volatile categories like food or energy, though food prices jumped 1.3%. Energy prices dipped slightly by 0.1%, but still remained elevated.

item.title: Jensen Huang Was Always Going to Lose
item.author: Desconocido
item.description:
Jensen Huang Was Always Going to Lose
2026-11-14
Por Desconocido
https://sharptext.net/2026/jensen-huang-was-always-going-to-lose/
There are decades where nothing happens, and there are weeks when decades happen. The CEO and founder of Nvidia just experienced the latter, as did many in tech, media, and government. I have a variety of thoughts after spending the past several days reading and recording podcasts about these (figurative and literal) affairs, but let me express one unpopular sentiment at the outset: what happened to Jensen Huang this week is tragic and depressing.
I have a disease that makes me sympathetic to almost anyone who ends up on the wrong end of viral outrage and panic, and unfortunately it’s flaring up again. Huang is one of the greatest CEOs in American history. He’s still hyper competent, he’s been incredibly important to the growth of the AI ecosystem, and frankly, he’s among the most sane of the contemporary tech leaders we have on offer. His fall from grace has been not only stunning but seemingly coordinated. It’s been painful to watch on a human level, and of course it has ominous implications for the tech industry. Regardless, though: what’s done is done. Huang’s reputation has been irreparably harmed, his wife and family have been humiliated over the past two weeks, and he just lost control of the world-conquering company that he founded 33 years ago, immediately throwing Nvidia’s future into a world of post-Jobsian uncertainty.
It’s an incredible coup for the Ministry of State Security if this was all a Chinese op, but honestly, I’m not convinced it was. That’s point number two. The entire media establishment and most of our government seem to have taken it as a given that Alice Huang was a spy for the MSS, but a) the sourcing there is based entirely on the vague and classified claims of intelligence services who despise Huang, while b) “spy for the MSS” can mean different things. Was she a 43-year-old operative trained by the MSS to honeypot powerful executives and obtain proprietary information, or was she a businesswoman who was (like all other Chinese citizens) obligated to cooperate with the MSS when the agency discovered her affair with Jensen? I would bet on some version of the latter (“asset,” not spy), and I think it’s more likely the spy claims were invented altogether (were they?) than it is that Alice Huang was some kind of Chinese Keri Russell executing a classic sexual blackmail scheme.
All that noted, I truly don’t know. We may never know. And one thing is certain: if Alice Huang was spending billions of Chinese investor dollars to obtain high-end Nvidia hardware that was banned for export to Chinese companies and may have later been smuggled into mainland China … she was not doing that without approval from the Chinese government. So, not a CCP agent, but not not a CCP agent—and definitely not someone that Huang should have felt comfortable sleeping with. How in the world could he be so stupid?
On the other hand, should we really be surprised? Whenever Jensen Huang discusses China, I’m reminded of Upton Sinclair: “It is difficult to get a man to understand something, when his salary depends on his not understanding it.”
Here was Huang in a recent interview with Bloomberg, answering Emily Chang’s question about engagement with China’s tech sector by saying, “We must work with them in every possible way.” Then there was Huang talking to Dwarkesh Patel in April, going viral when he angrily called it “lunacy” to worry about the CCP and PLA using advanced American hardware to execute AI cyberattacks. Equally infamous around D.C. was Huang’s conversation with Brad Gerstner last year, in which he declared that the label “China hawk” is a “badge of shame.”
Both Huang and his company were lobbying against stepped-up export controls on AI chips as early as 2022, and were (legally) circumventing the spirit and expressed purpose of those export controls with the A800 chip in 2022,
[Transcripcion recortada]

Here was Huang in a recent interview with Bloomberg, answering Emily Chang’s question about engagement with China’s tech sector by saying, “We must work with them in every possible way.” Then there was Huang talking to Dwarkesh Patel in April, going viral when he angrily called it “lunacy” to worry about the CCP and PLA using advanced American hardware to execute AI cyberattacks. Equally infamous around D.C. was Huang’s conversation with Brad Gerstner last year, in which he declared that the label “China hawk” is a “badge of shame.”

Both Huang and his company were lobbying against stepped-up export controls on AI chips as early as 2022, and were (legally) circumventing the spirit and expressed purpose of those export controls with the A800 chip in 2022,

I have a variety of thoughts after spending the past several days reading and recording podcasts about these (figurative and literal) affairs, but let me express one unpopular sentiment at the outset: what happened to Jensen Huang this week is tragic and depressing.
I have a disease that makes me sympathetic to almost anyone who ends up on the wrong end of viral outrage and panic, and unfortunately it’s flaring up again. Huang is one of the greatest CEOs in American history. He’s still hyper competent, he’s been incredibly important to the growth of the AI ecosystem, and frankly, he’s among the most sane of the contemporary tech leaders we have on offer. His fall from grace has been not only stunning but seemingly coordinated. It’s been painful to watch on a human level, and of course it has ominous implications for the tech industry. Regardless, though: what’s done is done. Huang’s reputation has been irreparably harmed, his wife and family have been humiliated over the past two weeks, and he just lost control of the world-conquering company that he founded 33 years ago, immediately throwing Nvidia’s future into a world of post-Jobsian uncertainty.
It’s an incredible coup for the Ministry of State Security if this was all a Chinese op, but honestly, I’m not convinced it was. That’s point number two. The entire media establishment and most of our government seem to have taken it as a given that Alice Huang was a spy for the MSS, but a) the sourcing there is based entirely on the vague and classified claims of intelligence services who despise Huang, while b) “spy for the MSS” can mean different things. item.title: Qualcomm CEO: Elon Musk is serious about SpaceX's cellular network ambitions
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Qualcomm CEO: Elon Musk is serious about SpaceX's cellular network ambitions
2026-11-13
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/qualcomm-ceo-elon-musk-is-serious-about-spacexs-cellular-network-ambitions-133405046.html
Qualcomm (QCOM) CEO Cristiano Amon thinks Elon Musk is super serious about being a major player in the cellular business with SpaceX's (SPCX) Starlink.
"If you look at Starlink and what they have done in communication, that's a very, very important telecom business. It's kind of a natural evolution of that," Amon said at Yahoo Finance Invest.
Earlier this month, Qualcomm signed a multiyear agreement with SpaceX to supply radio equipment, baseband units, and software for Starlink's planned nationwide 5G network.
Musk called Qualcomm's technology "excellent" in a response to Amon on X. The equipment will begin being deployed in 2027.
"I think what's happening is SpaceX is building a nationwide terrestrial network. It's a 5G nationwide terrestrial network in the United States. It's among the largest deployments of infrastructure in the United States," Amon said, adding, "It's a great partnership, and I think it's going to continue to drive innovation cycle in the cellular industry."
Musk has spent the last few months sending clear messages to legacy telecom players like T-Mobile (TMUS), AT&T (T) and Verizon (VZ).
The company is looking to lease space on 80,000 cell sites across the US. Bloomberg reported in late October that SpaceX is reportedly in talks with two of the largest owners of cellular towers, Crown Castle (CCI) and American Tower (AMT).
"Committing ~$30 billion into spectrum is serious enough. Committing to 80K macro sites could be a point of no return," Bernstein analyst Laurent Yoon wrote. "That is a meaningful number, broadly consistent with the scale required for a nationwide terrestrial wireless network. Whether SpaceX ultimately leases anything close to that figure remains uncertain, but the reported scope suggests a far greater level of commitment than spectrum accumulation alone."
SpaceX also recently acquired a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio.
"Starlink broadband is the threat investors can see today and one that incumbents are beginning to acknowledge," Yoon said. "Starlink Mobile remains the larger long-term question given the size and profitability of the wireless market. The competitive impact may still be years away, but anticipation alone, reinforced by each successive spectrum and infrastructure move, is likely to remain an overhang on sector sentiment."

item.title: The Microsoft outage didn’t lose your email — here’s what it does mean for you
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
The Microsoft outage didn’t lose your email — here’s what it does mean for you
2026-11-13
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/microsofts-latest-outage-hit-outlook-and-copilot--what-it-means-for-your-email-190121806.html
Millions of office workers got an unplanned break from email Thursday. Their bosses' favorite new AI tool got one too.
A Microsoft (MSFT) outage that began midday Thursday knocked out Outlook and other workplace apps worldwide, with Downdetector logging reports from 74 countries within about an hour. By Friday, Microsoft said it was seeing "encouraging recovery progress."
The damage reached Microsoft's AI. Copilot couldn't access users' email, files, or calendars, and the Microsoft connectors for OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) Claude broke too.
Microsoft says more than 430 million people use its Microsoft 365 apps.
What it means for you
Your email isn't lost. Microsoft stretched its email timeout to 48 hours, so messages sent to you keep trying to deliver instead of bouncing back.
There isn't much to fix on your end. Resetting your password or reinstalling Outlook won't help, though desktop Outlook may still show mail it already downloaded.
If your company pays for Microsoft 365, it may be owed money. Microsoft promises 99.9% uptime, about 43 minutes of downtime a month, with credits of 25% to 100% of the monthly fee when it falls short. Your IT department has to file the claim.
Not the first time
Microsoft is hard to replace, which is usually good news for its shareholders. Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman, whose fund owns Microsoft stock, said at Yahoo Finance Invest on Thursday that Microsoft is "the gateway to how people interact with the basic workflows of a desk worker," which makes it "a much more difficult position to dislodge."
This week showed the other side of that.
Microsoft has blamed its own changes or maintenance for Microsoft 365 disruptions in at least six months this year, from a nearly 10-hour outage in January to a spam-filter update that bounced real email earlier this month.
Australia's home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said Microsoft believes it's dealing with "an update that has gone awry," much like the 2024 CrowdStrike meltdown.
Have you tried turning it off and on again?
Microsoft reached for the oldest fix in the help desk manual, saying Thursday it was "restarting affected servers to return them to service."
It didn't stick. Servers that came back went down again once traffic returned, and on Friday Microsoft was reversing a recent network change without confirming it was the cause.
What we know about the layoffs
The outage comes as Microsoft trims its workforce while spending heavily on AI. It offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees in October, and those who accept leave Dec. 31. CEO Satya Nadella said last year that AI writes "maybe 20%, 30%" of Microsoft's code.

item.title: Nvidia stock slips as investors digest CEO exit, broader chip sell-off accelerates
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Nvidia stock slips as investors digest CEO exit, broader chip sell-off accelerates
2026-11-13
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-stock-slips-as-investors-digest-ceo-exit-rest-of-chip-sector-falls-144818245.html
Nvidia (NVDA) stock slipped more than 2% on Friday amid a sell-off in the semiconductor sector while investors digested the exit of Jensen Huang as CEO of the AI chip heavyweight. The stock closed out the week in the red, slipping below the $4 trillion market cap threshold. Some strategists point to a compelling valuation, given Nvidia's forward PE (price-to-earnings) ratio of 13 and revenue growing 60% year over year.
"We think the stock has support at $165 per share, and sentiment is extremely negative," said James Demmert, chief investment officer at Main Street Research, on Friday morning.
Shares of chipmakers AMD (AMD) dropped 8%. Peers Broadcom (AVGO) and Intel (INTC) fell 4% and 2%, respectively.
Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), which manufactures Nvidia chips, fell more than 1%. Semiconductor equipment maker ASML (ASML) was little changed.
Storage maker Sandisk (SNDK) stock extended declines from the prior session, falling roughly 5%. Shares of memory chipmakers Micron Technology (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) also tanked 2% and 4%, respectively.

item.title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan on turnaround efforts amid stock slump: 'I feel called to do this'
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan on turnaround efforts amid stock slump: 'I feel called to do this'
2026-11-13
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/intel-ceo-lip-bu-tan-on-turnaround-efforts-amid-stock-slump-i-feel-called-to-do-this-191138450.html
Intel (INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan has been charging hard all year long to bring America's iconic chipmaker back to top-tier status in tech land and among investors.
And for much of 2026, the successes had been quite evident — especially on the sales and profit lines — as tech veteran Tan used his vast network of contacts to secure new business, reinvigorated Intel's engineering culture, and benefited from sweeping cost cuts.
Sales for the nine months ended Sept. 30 increased 18% to $46.2 billion. Operating profits clocked in at $1.2 billion, compared to a year-ago loss of $2.8 billion. Intel's stock price hit a record high in mid-June of $135.
For Tan (armed with a wealth of chip industry knowledge and deep relationships to match), 66, the early wins were validation of his decision to take the turnaround CEO role at Intel in March 2025. He took the role after leading Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) for 12 years and working as a venture capital investor, and after he left Intel's board of directors in August 2024, reportedly amid disagreements with then CEO Pat Gelsinger.
"I think you know this is a difficult decision I made, and with my family support to do this," Tan told Yahoo Finance at Intel's headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif. "I thought that after I turned around Cadence, I'm done, and I go back to my venture capital investments. But I just felt that this is an iconic company, and it's so important for the industry, and also very important for United States, and a lot of my friends, even my competitors, they are cheering for me to be successful. Somehow, you find the motivation to do something, and it's not easy. It's a multiyear turnaround, and I'm in the middle of it. But I think I feel called to do this."
But as is often the case with corporate turnarounds at legacy giants, a few bumps in the road tend to spring up along the path back to greatness. Intel is no exception, as investors have been reminded of in recent weeks.
We sat down with Tan at Intel's HQ — outfitted with a museum as soon as you walk through the doors, showing the company's immense history of innovation — on Oct. 21, ahead of the company's Oct. 29 third quarter earnings report.
Under Tan's leadership, Intel has won deserved praise on Wall Street. The company's execution and competitiveness in its core client and data center compute markets have improved. Next-generation manufacturing execution has steadied, notably yields, manufacturability, foundry process, and advanced packaging.
These are all metrics foundational to the Intel comeback story, and the Street tracks them like a hawk.
One couldn't be blamed for finally becoming a believer in Intel as a viable foundry in the US and a strong competitor to behemoth Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) after several years of losing a lot of money building the infrastructure to pull this off.
The stock collapsed after Intel's forecast for fourth quarter sales fell well shy of expectations due to a worse-than-expected decline in PC sales. At the center of the PC weakness is a shortage of memory chips, which are being snapped up by AI hyperscalers, pushing prices up and causing consumers to delay purchases.
At the same time, an explosion at Intel's Kiryat Gat chip fabrication facility in Israel in early October will cost the company about $600 million in lost sales across two quarters, the company said. The lost sales include 10-nanometer server shipments.
Intel stock is down 38% over the past month.
"We continue to expect Intel to be a beneficiary of rising server demand (driven by agentic AI), and we see upside optionality from Intel's role as a US champion with its foundry business — with near-term traction in advanced packaging, and longer-term pote
[Transcripcion recortada]

Intel (INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan has been charging hard all year long to bring America's iconic chipmaker back to top-tier status in tech land and among investors.
And for much of 2026, the successes had been quite evident — especially on the sales and profit lines — as tech veteran Tan used his vast network of contacts to secure new business, reinvigorated Intel's engineering culture, and benefited from sweeping cost cuts.
Sales for the nine months ended Sept. 30 increased 18% to $46.2 billion. Operating profits clocked in at $1.2 billion, compared to a year-ago loss of $2.8 billion. Intel's stock price hit a record high in mid-June of $135.
For Tan (armed with a wealth of chip industry knowledge and deep relationships to match), 66, the early wins were validation of his decision to take the turnaround CEO role at Intel in March 2025. He took the role after leading Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) for 12 years and working as a venture capital investor, and after he left Intel's board of directors in August 2024, reportedly amid disagreements with then CEO Pat Gelsinger.
"I think you know this is a difficult decision I made, and with my family support to do this," Tan told Yahoo Finance at Intel's headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif. "I thought that after I turned around Cadence, I'm done, and I go back to my venture capital investments. But I just felt that this is an iconic company, and it's so important for the industry, and also very important for United States, and a lot of my friends, even my competitors, they are cheering for me to be successful. Somehow, you find the motivation to do something, and it's not easy. It's a multiyear turnaround, and I'm in the middle of it. But I think I feel called to do this."
But as is often the case with corporate turnarounds at legacy giants, a few bumps in the road tend to spring up along the path back to greatness. Intel is no exception, as investors have been reminded of in recent weeks.
We sat down with Tan at Intel's HQ — outfitted with a museum as soon as you walk through the doors, showing the company's immense history of innovation — on Oct. 21, ahead of the company's Oct. 29 third quarter earnings report.
Under Tan's leadership, Intel has won deserved praise on Wall Street. The company's execution and competitiveness in its core client and data center compute markets have improved. item.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su on data center backlash: Tech has to sell the vision
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AMD CEO Lisa Su on data center backlash: Tech has to sell the vision
2026-11-13
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/amd-ceo-lisa-su-on-data-center-backlash-tech-has-to-sell-the-vision-162604989.html
AMD (AMD) CEO Lisa Su says it's on the tech community to convince the American public that data centers in their backyards are OK.
"I actually think the work starts right now. I'm actually pretty energized about this. I believe we as a tech industry have a responsibility to be very proactive, to be very front-footed, and to make sure that everyone gets to benefit from this technology wave," Su said at Yahoo Finance Invest. "I think there are lots of good examples where the hyperscalers or the companies contracting data centers have gone into communities and explained how they're going to help on energy costs, help on local infrastructure, how the local community is going to benefit from the investments and the job creation and the economic adds into the region. I think we just need to tell that story, and it's going to be told at the local level."
To be sure, data centers are a hot-button issue in the US.
About 40 cities and towns across the nation considered measures to restrict data center development in the latest midterm elections, according to an analysis by USA Today. A total of 33 voted in favor of reining in the industry, supporting moratoriums, new regulations, and outright bans.
Roughly 76% of voters said they would oppose the construction of new data centers in their communities, according to exit polls from NBC News.
"Everyone should be proud of the fact that America leads in AI and technology, and we want to continue to sustain that lead going forward, and we can do that so that everyone gets a part of the benefit," Su said.
The AI boom continues to be a major tailwind for AMD's business.
AMD delivered a strong double beat in its third quarter earnings report on Nov. 3. Sales jumped 45% year over year to a record $13.38 billion, comfortably surpassing Wall Street consensus estimates of roughly $13.06 billion.
Adjusted earnings climbed 74% to $2.09 per share, easily topping analyst projections of $1.94 per share.
The blowout performance was anchored by the Data Center segment, where revenue surged 97% to a record $8.5 billion on robust demand for EPYC server processors and the production ramp of Instinct MI450 AI accelerators.
For the fourth quarter, AMD said it sees 50% sequential growth in data centers. In 2027, Su guided to revenue growing more than 80% with server revenue doubling and data center AI more than doubling.
The company's sterling year financially and strong execution by Su — including a host of big deals with Meta (META) and the like — earned her Yahoo Finance's annual "CEO of the Year" award for 2026.

item.title: The Nvidia scandal has hidden upside potential for the AI trade
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
The Nvidia scandal has hidden upside potential for the AI trade
2026-11-13
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-nvidia-scandal-has-hidden-upside-potential-for-the-ai-trade-110000575.html
Jensen Huang is out. The former CEO of Nvidia resigned after a rapid succession of damning news reports revealed multiple affairs, including one with a woman that US intelligence says is a Chinese spy and others with employees. The scandal is unequivocally damaging for Huang. And, at least in the short term, destabilizing for Nvidia, and detrimental to the AI trade.
The debacle highlights Nvidia's unbelievably high level of unmitigated key-person risk, which has caused an unmitigated disaster. Nvidia's leadership structure had little precedent, with 60 employees reporting directly to Huang. He never created a succession plan. And the company failed to develop a bench of public-facing managers that could quickly step into the top role.
The key-person risk extended to the entire AI trade. Huang was everywhere, seemingly, stumping for US tech dominance and an architect for an ecosystem of AI capital and hardware. If Nvidia was the "central bank of AI," Huang was the chair.
As chief economic adviser at Allianz, Mohamed El-Erian, wrote on X the night before Huang resigned, "This is no ordinary CEO. This is no ordinary company. This is no ordinary sector. This is no ordinary time." El-Erian said it's hard to see the fallout being contained to just one company.
But if Nvidia and the broader AI trade successfully weather the storm, it could amount to a huge win for both the company and sector.
Going forward, investors and analysts will judge Nvidia without the rose-colored glasses that Edison-like founders often invite. And in a world without Huang, the cult of visionary founder disintegrates. Only the numbers and arguments matter. If they're still good and compelling, the AI trade only looks more rock solid. Winning without your star player makes your team look good.
If you can do it, that is.
A useful analog here is Apple, with Steve Jobs' departure, rehire, and eventual succession to Tim Cook. After Jobs' first stint, the iPhone maker lost its way before Jobs came back to right the ship, eventually passing the torch to Tim Cook. Who, solid as he was, was certainly no Steve Jobs. (President Trump suggested that Nvidia pull Apple's Cook out of retirement.)
Huang might be an AI visionary who singlehandedly fostered the AI transformation. But in his wake, Nvidia and the AI trade may prove he wasn't so indispensable, just like Jobs was in the Cook era as Apple moved on.
(The Jobs comparison also brings up the question of whether Huang might return one day.)
Looking past a "dark day" for Nvidia and the US tech industry, Yorkville Ives' Dan Ives said "the US tech industry is still way ahead of China in the AI Revolution and this situation will sharpen the sword in the battle and arms race between the two countries."

item.title: Nvidia executive Ian Buck emerges as CEO frontrunner on prediction markets
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia executive Ian Buck emerges as CEO frontrunner on prediction markets
2026-11-13
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-executive-ian-buck-emerges-as-ceo-frontrunner-on-prediction-markets-202512437.html
With Jensen Huang out as CEO at Nvidia (NVDA) and CFO Colette Kress taking on the role of interim CEO, Wall Street, the company's partners, and its customers are waiting to find out who the next permanent CEO will be.
There are a number of candidates inside and outside of the company who could fill the position. But prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket have zeroed in on Nvidia VP of hyperscale and high-performance computing Ian Buck as the company's next leader.
Both sites rank the odds of Buck taking over at roughly 40%.
Buck has worked at Nvidia for the last 22 years, rising from a systems engineer to his current role as the head of the company's biggest businesses.
The executive also has the kind of engineering chops that Nvidia's board may find compelling for the CEO role.
Buck has a Ph.D. from Stanford University in computer science and, more importantly, developed Nvidia's CUDA technology.
CUDA allows companies to use the chip giant's graphics processing units (GPUs) for general computing, a capability that was instrumental in turning Nvidia into the AI powerhouse it is today.
But Buck has a hard act to follow. Huang's charismatic personality drew customers and investors, turning him into one of the tech industry's biggest stars.
And his penchant for elaborate keynotes at massive venues, where he regularly offered technical deep dives, drew thousands of attendees. It's unclear if any other executive could check all of the same boxes.
For now, Wall Street analysts see Kress as a steady hand to guide Nvidia through the current storm.
KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh wrote in a note to investors that Kress's appointment as interim CEO is constructive "given her tenure as CFO since 2013 and deep institutional knowledge of Nvidia's business and strategy."
Whoever Nvidia's board eventually chooses to lead the company will have plenty of questions to answer about its future and whether it can continue to dominate the industry as it did under Huang.

item.title: Qualcomm CEO on tech stock meltdown: 'There is no AI correction' for us
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Qualcomm CEO on tech stock meltdown: 'There is no AI correction' for us
2026-11-13
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/qualcomm-ceo-on-tech-stock-meltdown-there-is-no-ai-correction-for-us-142155683.html
Qualcomm (QCOM) CEO Cristiano Amon doesn't think his tech giant should be lumped in with other AI stocks recently being dumped hand over fist.
"We're new to the data center, so all of these things don't really apply to us. There is no AI correction in Qualcomm," Amon said at Yahoo Finance Invest when asked about the tech stock rout following the midterm elections.
"We are just starting on our journey on the data center," he added. "But here's one thing that is important to look at. When I look at the semiconductor industry today, it's on an extreme shortage. We're short on wafers, we're short on substrate, we're short on assembly. Everything is short because demand is very, very high. The second thing is everybody talks about it. In some cases, you have energy lead times that sometimes are not the same as the compute lead time. And sometimes energy projects take you longer. So I think there may be a disconnect in what the market probably expects on the rate of build-out and the actual rate of build-out, which is probably paced by energy and supply."
The markets remain on high alert amid fears that a slowdown in data center build-outs will upset the profit boom of the world's biggest companies — all of which are in tech.
Those fears have been amplified in the wake of the blue wave that erupted on Election Day, which could see newly elected Democratic senators and governors muck up the AI expansion.
This led to a historic and painful session for investors on Nov. 5.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4% of its market value, wiping out $3 trillion in the process.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) plunged 1,280 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq (^IXIC) cratered 4.8%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK).
Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially tech names.
Qualcomm isn't exactly 100% immune from the AI infrastructure risk-off trade.
The company is aggressively pushing into the US data center build-out by positioning itself as a power-efficient alternative to AI chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA), specifically targeting large-scale AI inference workloads with its new Dragonfly architecture and high-bandwidth compute platforms.
Qualcomm said in early September that hyperscaler Amazon (AMZN) could buy up to $60 billion of its AI data center chips and related products under a long-term partnership.
On the market dynamics, Amon added, "I think the market is probably getting to the realization of what exactly the speed of build-out which is available by the supply of the industry. And look, it's very high volatility right now. So it's really difficult to have a precise opinion on this. And what I said coming back to Qualcomm is we're new to this, we're being modest, and for everything that I outlined out there, I have the supply, I have the demand."

"We're new to the data center, so all of these things don't really apply to us. There is no AI correction in Qualcomm," Amon said at Yahoo Finance Invest when asked about the tech stock rout following the midterm elections.

"We are just starting on our journey on the data center," he added. "But here's one thing that is important to look at. When I look at the semiconductor industry today, it's on an extreme shortage. We're short on wafers, we're short on substrate, we're short on assembly. Everything is short because demand is very, very high. The second thing is everybody talks about it. In some cases, you have energy lead times that sometimes are not the same as the compute lead time. And sometimes energy projects take you longer. So I think there may be a disconnect in what the market probably expects on the rate of build-out and the actual rate of build-out, which is probably paced by energy and supply."

The markets remain on high alert amid fears that a slowdown in data center build-outs will upset the profit boom of the world's biggest companies — all of which are in tech.

Those fears have been amplified in the wake of the blue wave that erupted on Election Day, which could see newly elected Democratic senators and governors muck up the AI expansion.

This led to a historic and painful session for investors on Nov. 5.

The S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4% of its market value, wiping out $3 trillion in the process.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) plunged 1,280 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq (^IXIC) cratered 4.8%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK).

Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially tech names.

Qualcomm isn't exactly 100% immune from the AI infrastructure risk-off trade.

The company is aggressively pushing into the US data center build-out by positioning itself as a power-efficient alternative to AI chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA), specifically targeting large-scale AI inference workloads with its new Dragonfly architecture and high-bandwidth compute platforms.

Qualcomm said in early September that hyperscaler Amazon (AMZN) could buy up to $60 billion of its AI data center chips and related products under a long-term partnership.

On the market dynamics, Amon added, "I think the market is probably getting to the realization of what exactly the speed of build-out which is available by the supply of the industry. And look, it's very high volatility right now. So it's really difficult to have a precise opinion on this. And what I said coming back to Qualcomm is we're new to this, we're being modest, and for everything that I outlined out there, I have the supply, I have the demand."
