item.title: CoreWeave stock sinks as resignation of Jensen Huang ripples through AI trade
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
CoreWeave stock sinks as resignation of Jensen Huang ripples through AI trade
2026-11-13
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/coreweave-stock-sinks-as-resignation-of-jensen-huang-ripples-through-ai-trade-180319031.html
CoreWeave (CRWV) stock dropped nearly 7% after trimming losses on Thursday as the fallout from Nvidia's leadership change rippled through the AI trade.
Nvidia (NVDA), which owns more than 10% of CoreWeave and is a major chip supplier to the AI infrastructure provider, is facing heightened scrutiny as the board announced Jensen Huang would resign immediately and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
CoreWeave stock has been volatile in recent weeks amid concerns about AI financing. Those fears appeared to ease on Wednesday after the company posted better-than-expected quarterly results and said it does not plan to take on more expensive debt through 2027.
Shares of other Nvidia partners have also come under pressure on Thursday.
Super Micro Computer (SMCI) stock plunged more than 11% as Semafor reported widening scrutiny of Nvidia amid multiple US Justice Department investigations.
The report said one of the probes, on antitrust grounds, focuses on Nvidia, while the other two target AI infrastructure procurement firm Megaspeed and Super Micro. The California-based company makes AI servers which are stacked with Nvidia chips.

item.title: Fed releases meeting schedule for 2027, will not hold policy meeting next October
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed releases meeting schedule for 2027, will not hold policy meeting next October
2026-11-13
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-releases-meeting-schedule-for-2027-will-not-hold-policy-meeting-next-october-184022755.html
The Federal Reserve will not hold a policy meeting next October as part of a revised tentative schedule of policy meetings in 2027 released Thursday.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced last month that the interest-rate-setting committee would continue to meet eight times next year, but would scale back the number of policy meetings to seven, with one left for discussing broad monetary policy strategy issues. At the strategy meeting, there will be neither a vote on interest rates nor a policy statement released.
"Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular, and information-rich intervals," Warsh told reporters last month. "But it's equally important we reserve time and space, as an intellectually diverse group, for strategic deliberations — for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons."
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
This is the first step in eventually scaling back the number of policy meetings to six — an idea the Fed chairman floated this summer that the rest of the Fed supports because it will allow time to collect a fuller set of data to make more informed decisions about interest rates.
Warsh expects that in 2028, the Fed will have two meetings dedicated to discussions of strategy and six for setting policy.
The change comes as the Fed increasingly finds itself receiving key data after it sets interest rates. Last month, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index was released on Oct. 29, the day after the Fed met. The PCE index was released within days after the April and July meetings as well. The December meeting will take place the day before the November Consumer Price Index report is released.
While they can use pieces of other inflation datasets to estimate this measure, if the central bank met every eight weeks instead of the current six, it would have a fuller set of data available at each meeting.
"The current calendar has clear drawbacks," Deutsche Bank chief US economist Matt Luzzetti previously told Yahoo Finance. "The Fed could meaningfully improve the timeliness of the data available to them at FOMC meetings with relatively simple tweaks to the calendar."

item.title: We are in the middle of the digital renaissance, please take advantage of it
item.author: DAN KOE
item.description:
We are in the middle of the digital renaissance, please take advantage of it
2026-11-12
Por DAN KOE
https://letters.thedankoe.com/p/we-are-in-the-middle-of-the-digital
There will be 3 types of people in the future.
And the divide between them is growing larger every day.
If you want to win in the next 10 years, it is critical that you avoid becoming number 1 or 2.
1) The Purists
“We’re the ones who stayed clean.”
The ones who rejected AI and retreated into nature, simplicity, and screen-free living.
It’s a peaceful existence, until they come across someone who uses any form of technology, then they have an uncontrollable violent reaction because it threatens their identification with this new religion.
When you look at a purist, you can’t tell if they’re being serious or if they’re just doing it because it’s the rebellious and cool thing to do.
2) The Automatons
The ones who outsource every decision.
They’re allergic to friction and addicted to optimization. If their eyes aren’t glued to a screen, they feel as if they are losing an imaginary race. Every thought they have runs through Claude.
They don’t know where AI ends and where life begins.
Most people think they have to pick a side.
But I like to be different from most people. Maybe it’s a character flaw. Maybe it sounds cringe. But I find joy in it. It’s a creative challenge to live a life that very few people live, but I’ve found that growth (and therefore meaning/fulfillment) does not come from following the herd.
I’m convinced both sides are wrong.
The Purists reject an entire portion of reality (external progress), demonize it, and assume that it can’t be healthily integrated with prioritization and effort.
There are 4 quadrants of reality.
Like a skill tree in a video game.
You put points in each as you gain experience and increase your level. They interconnect. You can try to max out your money, but if you haven’t improved your mind, body, or spirit at all... money can only go so far. The greatest fruits of life await those who accept the challenge of continuous development in all domains of life.
The Purists treat their internal world (mind and spirit) as the highest truth and reject the external world.
This is a recipe for disaster.
It does not matter how enlightened you are. If your body is frail, health is at stake, and you don’t have any money to your name - you will suffer unnecessarily, and the solution to your problems is something you consider evil, so you have no choice but to play victim.
The Automatons, on the other hand, do the complete opposite. They obsess over money and progress until their humanity is nowhere to be found.
There is a 3rd option, however.
It sounds crazy and impossible to those who can’t think for themselves, but the future belongs to those who become multi-dimensional.
Here is how you win in the next 10 years:
The Digital Renaissance Man: Why Polymaths Win In The AI Age
We’re in the middle of the second renaissance where proof of work replaces the resume, an audience replaces the employer, and taste replaces credentials.
The greatest tragedy of our times is that we were fooled into believing that the Mechanical Life is the only path to success.
You were told to pick a lane.
You were convinced that having multiple interests was a character flaw.
Become a designer. Become a writer. Become an engineer, a marketer, a salesman, or just get whatever high-paying job you can because that’s how you become respected and live a good life.
And that seemed reasonable, but now you feel replaceable.
Because that was never how humans were meant to live.
The modern version of a “job” is only about 250 years old.
Before it, the ideal was a free person who did many things throughout their life (compared to a slave who did one specialized task... sounds familiar). The artisan, farmer, and pirate are all examples of those who knew how to run an entire operation, not just one piece of it. They were both the thinker a
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Winners and Losers From AI Agents
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Winners and Losers From AI Agents
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
Winners and Losers From AI Agents
Key Takeaways
An estimated $30 trillion in consumer spending could be digitized through agentic AI offerings across multiple industries.
As AI agents increasingly influence purchasing decisions, operational efficiency, pricing and digital capabilities may become more important than traditional advantages such as brand recognition.
AI agents could make it easier for consumers to compare products and services, intensifying competition in industries such as insurance, auto retail and ticket resale.
By simplifying discovery, booking and transactions, AI agents could increase the use of software for such industries as transportation, local services and insurance.
Established retailers with trusted customer relationships, competitive prices and reliable delivery networks may be better positioned to withstand disruption.
The recent launch of powerful consumer AI agents has reignited debate over how artificial intelligence could disrupt industries ranging from retail and insurance to transportation and live entertainment.
Unlike traditional AI tools that primarily answer questions, these agents can browse websites, complete forms, compare prices, make purchases and even help negotiate bills.
Morgan Stanley Research estimates that roughly $30 trillion in consumer spending could be digitized through AI agents across online advertising, e-commerce, travel, food delivery, ridesharing, logistics, wearables and other sectors.
The extent of the disruption will depend on how quickly consumers adopt AI agents and how effectively companies make money from agent-driven activity and transactions.
“We continue to believe leading tech platforms with broad-based reach and unique data sets are in advantaged positions to create unique consumer agentic offerings that drive utility and garner scaled adoption,” says Brian Nowak, head of U.S. Internet Research at Morgan Stanley.
For investors, the implications vary widely by industry. While AI agents could increase demand for certain services and make transaction more efficient, they could also intensify price competition, weaken traditional advantages in winning customers and shift advertising revenue toward new platforms.

“We continue to believe leading tech platforms with broad-based reach and unique data sets are in advantaged positions to create unique consumer agentic offerings that drive utility and garner scaled adoption,” says Brian Nowak, head of U.S. Internet Research at Morgan Stanley.

For investors, the implications vary widely by industry. While AI agents could increase demand for certain services and make transaction more efficient, they could also intensify price competition, weaken traditional advantages in winning customers and shift advertising revenue toward new platforms.

item.title: AI Investing After the Midterms Dip
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
AI Investing After the Midterms Dip
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
AI Investing After the Midterms Dip
Key Takeaways
The selloff in AI-related stocks after the U.S. midterms appeared overdone, and markets have since recovered some of the losses; and further volatility could create potential buying opportunities.
Some data center projects scheduled for 2028 could move to 2029, potentially supporting a smoother rebalance between supply and demand across the supply chain.
Morgan Stanley Research maintains its forecasts for hyperscaler capital spending of $1.6 trillion in 2028 and $1.8 trillion in 2029.
Financing could become more selective, with increasing importance given to tenant quality, access to power and contractual protections.
The main investment opportunities after the selloff include the hyperscalers, select data center supply chain companies, software enablers and AI adopters.
Equity markets, particularly technology stocks, fell sharply in the days after the U.S. midterm elections. Democrats’ sizable advantage in both the House and Senate, alongside gains in several governors’ races, raised investor questions about the outlook for data center construction, the technology investment cycle and global equities. Markets have since recovered some of the losses from that initial post-election selloff.
However, Morgan Stanley Research believes the selloff was an overreaction. Should there be further volatility, investors can look for opportunities among AI enablers, infrastructure providers and companies adopting the technology.
The election results are more likely to delay some data center projects from 2028 to 2029 than derail the broader capital investment cycle. This has potential to elongate the AI spending cycle, which could bring a smoother rebalancing of supply and demand across the data center supply chain, an improved credit outlook and higher lease rates for computing capacity.
More than 20 Morgan Stanley Research teams globally assessed how the new U.S. political landscape could affect data center development, policy and equity investment opportunities across the U.S., Asia and Europe.
1. Data Center Buildout Delayed, Not Derailed
Newly elected governors are unlikely to disrupt projects already under construction, leaving the outlook for 2027 projects unchanged. However, some data centers scheduled for completion in Texas and Ohio in 2028 could be delayed until 2029 as incoming governors work with legislators to establish new requirements for developers.
Morgan Stanley Research has shifted 20% of its projected 2028 data center capacity to 2029, while maintaining a positive view of the overall buildout. Globally, the revised forecast implies growth in data center capacity of 9% in 2028 and 20% in 2029.
Potential U.S. delays could also create attractive opportunities for data center development outside the country.
2. AI Capital Spending Forecast Stays on Track
Hyperscalers—the major technology companies providing cloud computing, storage and networking services—are likely to continue spending and building as much capacity as possible to develop and scale new products for billions of users. The reason is simple: AI investment continues to offer an estimated return on invested capital of more than 30%.
Morgan Stanley Research maintains its forecasts for hyperscaler capital spending of $1.6 trillion in 2028 and $1.8 trillion in 2029.
These companies are also likely to shift some development to states with more favorable policies toward data centers, including Tennessee and Louisiana.
3. Financing Remains Available But Selective
With capital spending forecasts unchanged, AI-related debt issuance is likely to remain high in 2027, led by the hyperscalers.
However, financing for new construction and specialized AI cloud providers, known as neoclouds, could face greater scrutiny. Tenant quality, a credible path to securing power and contractual protections will likely become increasingly important.
